  4. मम्मी अभी खाना बना रही हैं। (mummy abhee khaanaa banaa rahee hain.)

Phone roleplay — actually sit in different rooms and call (or video-call) each other. Script: greet; ask क्या कर रहे हो / कर रही हो?; both invent answers (bonus for absurd ones: मैं डोसा बना रहा हूँ!); each report what two other people are "doing" right now — one elder each, respect plural enforced; one sound-effects round: make a noise, other asks यह क्या आवाज़ है?; close with तुम्हारी याद आ रही है and hang up like a Bollywood scene. Swap who calls first.
chapters.book4-L07:
Lesson 7 Ordering Food & Likes

Saturday evening food crawl: first the legendary momos cart outside Lajpat Nagar market — steamer hissing, red chutney glowing like a warning light — then dinner at a little Punjabi restaurant where the waiter has already decided what you should eat. Tonight Jacob learns the most useful sentence in India: how to say he likes something.

Big unlock: in Hindi you don't "like" things — things "are pleasing TO you". The liker takes ko: मुझे (mujhe) "to me", तुम्हें (tumhen) [tum-hay(n)] "to you", आपको (aapko) "to you (polite)". So: मुझे मोमोज़ पसंद हैं = "to me, momos are pleasing." Same skeleton for needing: मुझे पानी चाहिए "to me, water is needed." The whole ko-family lives in Unit 10.

Dialogue, part one: at the momos cart

Priya:
जैकब, तुम्हें मोमोज़ पसंद हैं?
Jacob, tumhen momos pasand hain? [jay-kub, tum-hay(n) moh-mohz puh-sund heh(n)]
Jacob, do you like momos?
Jacob:
पसंद? मुझे मोमोज़ बहुत पसंद हैं!
pasand? mujhe momos bahut pasand hain! [puh-sund? mu-jhay moh-mohz bo-hut puh-sund heh(n)]
Like? I LOVE momos!
Priya:
भैया, एक प्लेट वेज मोमोज़ देना।
bhaiyaa, ek pleT vej momos denaa. [bheh-yah, ayk playT vayj moh-mohz day-nah]
Bhaiya, one plate of veg momos please.
Momos-vaalaa:
चटनी? तीखी चटनी?
chaTnee? teekhee chaTnee? [chuT-nee? tee-khee chuT-nee]
Chutney? Spicy chutney?
Jacob:
हाँ जी… थोड़ी।
haan jee… thoRee. [hah(n) jee… thoh-Ree]
Yes… a little.
Priya:
भैया, तीखा कम! यह अमेरिकन हैं!
bhaiyaa, teekhaa kam! yeh amerikan hain! [bheh-yah, tee-khah kum! yeh uh-may-ri-kun heh(n)]
Bhaiya, less spice! This one's American! (mock-formal हैं — maximum teasing)
Momos-vaalaa:
(laughing) ठीक है जी! लो — गरम मोमोज़!
Theek hai jee! lo — garam momos! [Theek heh jee! loh — guh-rum moh-mohz]
Okay ji! Here — hot momos!
Jacob:
अरे बाप रे! तीखा है! भैया, पानी चाहिए!
arre baap re! teekhaa hai! bhaiyaa, paanee chaahiye! [uh-ray bahp ray! tee-khah heh! bheh-yah, pah-nee chah-hi-yay]
Good grief! It's spicy! Bhaiya, I need water!

Dialogue, part two: at the restaurant

Waiter:
जी, क्या चाहिए?
jee, kyaa chaahiye? [jee, kyah chah-hi-yay]
Yes — what would you like? (lit. what is needed?)
Priya:
मेन्यू चाहिए, भैया।
menyoo chaahiye, bhaiyaa. [may-nyoo chah-hi-yay, bheh-yah]
We need a menu, bhaiya.
Waiter:
यह लीजिए। आज छोले-भटूरे बहुत अच्छे हैं।
yeh leejiye. aaj chhole-bhaToore bahut achchhe hain. [yeh lee-ji-yeh. ahj chhoh-lay-bhuh-Too-ray bo-hut uch-chhay heh(n)]
Here you are. The chhole bhature are very good today.
Jacob:
मुझे छोले-भटूरे पसंद हैं! और प्रिया को पनीर पसंद है।
mujhe chhole-bhaToore pasand hain! aur Priya ko paneer pasand hai. [mu-jhay chhoh-lay-bhuh-Too-ray puh-sund heh(n)! awr pri-yah koh puh-neer puh-sund heh]
I like chhole bhature! And Priya likes paneer.
Priya:
हाँ — शाही पनीर और दो रोटी चाहिए।
haan — shaahee paneer aur do roTee chaahiye. [hah(n) — shah-hee puh-neer awr doh roh-Tee chah-hi-yay]
Yes — we'd like shahi paneer and two rotis.
Waiter:
और पीने के लिए? कुछ चाहिए?
aur peene ke liye? kuchh chaahiye? [awr pee-nay kay li-yay? kuchh chah-hi-yay]
And to drink? Anything? (lit. for drinking)
Jacob:
एक लस्सी और एक पानी, बस।
ek lassee aur ek paanee, bas. [ayk lus-see awr ayk pah-nee, bus]
One lassi and one water, that's all.
Waiter:
बिल्कुल जी! अभी लाता हूँ।
bilkul jee! abhee laataa hoon. [bil-kul jee! uh-bhee lah-tah hoo(n)]
Absolutely! I'll bring it right away. (lit. right-now I bring)

Momos arrived with Delhi's Tibetan and Nepali communities and conquered the city; every market now has a cart, and the fluorescent red chutney has its own fan clubs and casualty lists. Order like a local: वेज or चिकन (chikan) [chi-kun], स्टीम (sTeem) [sTeem] or फ़्राइड (fraaiD) [frah-iD]. And when the heat hits, the honest cry is exactly Jacob's: अरे बाप रे! — "oh father!" — Delhi's all-purpose expression of shock.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
मुझे … पसंद है।mujhe … pasand hai.mu-jhay … puh-sund hehI like … (one thing)
मुझे मोमोज़ पसंद हैं।mujhe momos pasand hain.mu-jhay moh-mohz puh-sund heh(n)I like momos. (plural → hain!)
तुम्हें क्या पसंद है?tumhen kyaa pasand hai?tum-hay(n) kyah puh-sund hehWhat do you like? (casual)
आपको क्या पसंद है?aapko kyaa pasand hai?ahp-koh kyah puh-sund hehWhat do you like? (polite)
क्या चाहिए?kyaa chaahiye?kyah chah-hi-yayWhat do you need / would you like?
मुझे पानी चाहिए।mujhe paanee chaahiye.mu-jhay pah-nee chah-hi-yayI need water.
तीखा / तीखा कमteekhaa / teekhaa kamtee-khah / tee-khah kumspicy / less spicy
चटनीchaTnee (f)chuT-neechutney
एक प्लेट मोमोज़ek pleT momos (f)ayk playT moh-mohzone plate of momos
मेन्यूmenyoo (m)may-nyoomenu
रोटीroTee (f)roh-Teeroti, flatbread
लस्सीlassee (f)lus-seelassi (sweet yogurt drink)

The English "I like momos" tempts you into मैं मोमोज़ पसंद हूँ — which announces that YOU are pleasing to momos. Flip it: liker + ko, thing as subject: मुझे मोमोज़ पसंद हैं। And match the verb to the THING: पनीर पसंद है (one), मोमोज़ पसंद हैं (many). चाहिए is easier — Delhi speech keeps it चाहिए for singular and plural alike: दो रोटी चाहिए।

Restaurant food is communal: dishes land in the middle and everyone shares — ordering "your own" main course marks you as a tourist. The waiter's recommendation (आज … बहुत अच्छे हैं) is usually genuine intelligence, not upselling. And your host will pile seconds onto your plate; the polite defense is बस, बस! with both hands over the plate — which buys you, at most, ten seconds.

Did you catch that?

Exercise 7A — Comprehension

Answer in Hindi — short answers are fine. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 7.

  1. जैकब को क्या बहुत पसंद है? (Jacob ko kyaa bahut pasand hai?)
  2. चटनी कैसी है? (chaTnee kaisee hai?)
  3. प्रिया को क्या पसंद है? (Priya ko kyaa pasand hai?)
  4. कितनी रोटी चाहिए? (kitnee roTee chaahiye?)
  5. पीने के लिए क्या चाहिए? (peene ke liye kyaa chaahiye?)

Pattern practice

One skeleton, two verbs. Person + ko — thing — पसंद है/हैं or चाहिए:

To whomThingEnding
मुझे (mujhe)चायपसंद है। (pasand hai.)
तुम्हें (tumhen)मोमोज़पसंद हैं? (pasand hain?)
आपको (aapko)क्याचाहिए? (chaahiye?)
प्रिया को / हमें (Priya ko / hamen)पानीचाहिए। (chaahiye.)

Exercise 7B — Likes and needs

Build a full sentence from each cue. Watch है vs हैं after पसंद. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 7.

  1. मैं / मोमोज़ — like (main / momos)
  2. मैं / चाय — like (main / chaay)
  3. तुम / पनीर — ask "do you like…?" (tum / paneer)
  4. आप / दिल्ली — ask "do you like…?" (aap / dillee)
  5. प्रिया / लस्सी — like (Priya / lassee)
  6. मैं / पानी — need (main / paanee)
  7. हम / मेन्यू — need (ham → hamen / menyoo)
  8. मम्मी / चाय — like (mummy / chaay)

Translation practice

Exercise 7C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 7.

  1. I like momos.
  2. I need water.
  3. Do you like paneer? (tum)
  4. Bhaiya, less spicy please!

Exercise 7D — Into English

Write the English meaning. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 7.

  1. आपको क्या चाहिए? (aapko kyaa chaahiye?)
  2. प्रिया को चाय पसंद है। (Priya ko chaay pasand hai.)
  3. मुझे छोले-भटूरे बहुत पसंद हैं। (mujhe chhole-bhaToore bahut pasand hain.)
  4. क्या तुम्हें दिल्ली पसंद है? (kyaa tumhen dillee pasand hai?)

Menu night. Grab a delivery app or a takeout menu and order dinner entirely in Hindi: your partner is the waiter (जी, क्या चाहिए?), you order two dishes and drinks (… चाहिए), declare one like and one dislike (मुझे … पसंद है / पसंद नहीं है), and negotiate the spice level (तीखा कम!). Then the lightning round: partner names ten foods rapid-fire; for each you answer instantly with पसंद है! / पसंद हैं! / नहीं! Get the है/हैं wrong and the imaginary waiter brings you extra-spicy chutney.
chapters.book4-L08:
Lesson 8 Prices, Numbers & Time

Sunday, Sarojini Nagar market — Delhi's great bargain jungle. Vendors chant prices over mountains of kurtas, lanes are packed shoulder to shoulder, and everything is negotiable except the crowd. Jacob wants a kurta; Priya wants to see him ask prices himself. At 6:30 they're meeting Kabir at Dilli Haat — which means a race to the metro token counter.

Numbers 0–100 get their full chapter in Book 3 — today is the field kit: round numbers, prices, and clock time. Three golden words: डेढ़ (DeRh) [DayRh] = one and a half, ढाई (Dhaaee) [Dhah-ee] = two and a half, and साढ़े (saaRhe) [sah-Rhay] = "plus a half" for 3½ up. Hindi never says "three-thirty" — it says "half-more-than-three": साढ़े तीन बजे.

Numbers you need today

1–10TensHalves & time
एक (ek) 1 · दो (do) 2 · तीन (teen) 3 · चार (chaar) 4 · पाँच (paanch) 5दस (das) 10 · बीस (bees) 20 · तीस (tees) 30 · चालीस (chaalees) 40 · पचास (pachaas) 50डेढ़ (DeRh) 1½ · ढाई (Dhaaee) 2½ · साढ़े चार (saaRhe chaar) 4½
छह (chheh) 6 · सात (saat) 7 · आठ (aaTh) 8 · नौ (nau) 9साठ (saaTh) 60 · सत्तर (sattar) 70 · अस्सी (assee) 80 · नब्बे (nabbe) 90 · सौ (sau) 100डेढ़ सौ (DeRh sau) 150 · ढाई सौ (Dhaaee sau) 250 · … बजे (… baje) o'clock

Say them: ek [ayk] · do [doh] · teen [teen] · chaar [chahr] · paanch [pah(n)ch] · chheh [chheh] · saat [saht] · aaTh [ahTh] · nau [naw] · das [dus] · bees [bees] · tees [tees] · chaalees [chah-lees] · pachaas [puh-chahs] · saaTh [sahTh] · sattar [sut-tur] · assee [us-see] · nabbe [nub-bay] · sau [saw] · baje [buh-jay].

Dialogue, part one: the Sarojini stall

Vendor:
आइए मैडम! आइए सर! सब सौ-सौ!
aaiye maiDam! aaiye sar! sab sau-sau! [ah-i-yay meh-Dum! ah-i-yay sur! sub saw-saw]
Come, madam! Come, sir! Everything a hundred each!
Jacob:
भैया, यह कुर्ता कितने का है?
bhaiyaa, yeh kurtaa kitne kaa hai? [bheh-yah, yeh kur-tah kit-nay kah heh]
Bhaiya, how much is this kurta?
Vendor:
दो सौ रुपये।
do sau rupaye. [doh saw ru-puh-yay]
Two hundred rupees.
Jacob:
दो सौ? और वह नीला कुर्ता?
do sau? aur voh neelaa kurtaa? [doh saw? awr voh nee-lah kur-tah]
Two hundred? And that blue kurta?
Vendor:
वह भी दो सौ। दोनों — तीन सौ पचास!
voh bhee do sau. donon — teen sau pachaas! [voh bhee doh saw. doh-noh(n) — teen saw puh-chahs]
That one's two hundred too. Both — three fifty!
Priya:
(quietly, to Jacob) तीन सौ ठीक है।
teen sau Theek hai. [teen saw Theek heh]
Three hundred is fair.
Jacob:
भैया… तीन सौ?
bhaiyaa… teen sau? [bheh-yah… teen saw]
Bhaiya… three hundred? (the raised eyebrow does the bargaining)
Vendor:
अच्छा चलो जी, तीन सौ — बस आपके लिए!
achchhaa chalo jee, teen sau — bas aapke liye! [uch-chhah chuh-loh jee, teen saw — bus ahp-kay li-yay]
Oh fine, three hundred — just for you!

Dialogue, part two: the clock and the token counter

Jacob:
प्रिया, अभी कितने बजे हैं?
Priya, abhee kitne baje hain? [pri-yah, uh-bhee kit-nay buh-jay heh(n)]
Priya, what time is it right now?
Priya:
साढ़े पाँच। और साढ़े छह बजे कबीर दिल्ली हाट आ रहा है!
saaRhe paanch. aur saaRhe chheh baje Kabir dillee haaT aa rahaa hai! [sah-Rhay pah(n)ch. awr sah-Rhay chheh buh-jay kuh-beer dil-lee hahT ah ruh-hah heh]
Five-thirty. And at six-thirty Kabir is coming to Dilli Haat!
Jacob:
अरे! चलो, मेट्रो!
arre! chalo, meTro! [uh-ray! chuh-loh, may-troh]
Yikes! Come on, metro!
Jacob:
(at the counter) भैया, दो टोकन देना — आई.एन.ए.।
bhaiyaa, do Tokan denaa — INA. [bheh-yah, doh Toh-kun day-nah — ah-ee-en-ay]
Bhaiya, two tokens please — INA (station).
Clerk:
चालीस रुपये।
chaalees rupaye. [chah-lees ru-puh-yay]
Forty rupees.
Jacob:
यह लीजिए — सौ।
yeh leejiye — sau. [yeh lee-ji-yeh — saw]
Here you are — a hundred.
Clerk:
और यह साठ रुपये वापस।
aur yeh saaTh rupaye vaapas. [awr yeh sahTh ru-puh-yeh vah-pus]
And here's sixty rupees back.
Priya:
शाबाश! अब तुम बिल्कुल दिल्ली-वाले हो!
shaabaash! ab tum bilkul dillee-vaale ho! [shah-bahsh! ub tum bil-kul dil-lee-vah-lay hoh]
Bravo! Now you're a total Delhi guy!

Sarojini survival guide: the chant सब सौ-सौ! means "everything ₹100 each" — doubling a number distributes it. The buyer's superpower is asking कितने का है? and then just… walking away slowly; prices fall like Delhi's winter sun. Real bargaining verbs come in Lesson 11 — until then, Jacob's move (repeat a lower number with a question mark) is a legitimate national technique. At the metro, though, prices are sacred: nobody bargains with the DMRC.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
यह कितने का है?yeh kitne kaa hai?yay kit-nay kah hehHow much is this? (m. thing)
यह कितने की है?yeh kitne kee hai?yay kit-nay kee hehHow much is this? (f. thing)
… रुपये… rupaye (m)ru-puh-yay… rupees
सस्ता / महँगाsastaa / mehngaasus-tah / meh(n)-gahcheap / expensive
दोनोंdonondoh-noh(n)both
कितने बजे हैं?kitne baje hain?kit-nay buh-jay heh(n)What time is it?
पाँच बजे हैं।paanch baje hain.pah(n)ch buh-jay heh(n)It's five o'clock.
साढ़े पाँच बजेsaaRhe paanch bajesah-Rhay pah(n)ch buh-jay(at) half past five
डेढ़ बजा है। / ढाई बजे हैं।DeRh bajaa hai. / Dhaaee baje hain.DayRh buh-jah heh / Dhah-ee buh-jay heh(n)It's 1:30. / It's 2:30.
कितने बजे … ?kitne baje … ?kit-nay buh-jayat what time … ?
टोकनTokan (m)Toh-kunmetro token
वापसvaapasvah-pusback (change, returns)

Two agreement traps. Price questions agree with the item: कुर्ता कितने का है? but चाय कितने की है? and plural कुर्ते कितने के हैं? Clock times: 1 o'clock and 1:30 are grammatically singular — एक बजा है, डेढ़ बजा है (bajaa hai) — everything from 2 up takes बजे हैं. But "AT a time" is always plain बजे: डेढ़ बजे = at 1:30.

Bargaining is theatre, not combat: smile, sigh, admire the goods, quote your number like a fond hope. The vendor's बस आपके लिए! ("only for you!") has been said to every customer since morning — enjoy it anyway. Where prices are printed (metro, malls, medicine), bargaining is out of place. And a hundred-rupee note at a small stall beats a two-thousand note every single time.

Did you catch that?

Home shopping channel: your partner lays out five household objects with secret prices and plays a Sarojini vendor (chant included: सब सौ-सौ!). You ask यह कितने का है? / कितने की है? for each, react — महँगा है! or सस्ता! — and buy two things with imaginary notes, checking your change (… रुपये वापस). Then the clock game: partner says random times in Hindi, you set them on a phone clock; swap. Last round is the daily-life quiz: तुम कितने बजे उठते हो? कितने बजे सोते हो? — answer honestly. The morning claims from Lesson 5 will now face mathematical scrutiny.

chapters.book4-L09:
Lesson 9 Talking About Yesterday

The scene: Sunday evening at home. Jacob spent yesterday wandering Old Delhi with a friend while his partner Priya was at her cousin's place. Now they trade notes about the day — and slide into childhood memories. This lesson runs on the past forms of होना honaa [hoh-nah] — था / थी / थे / थीं thaa / thee / the / theen [thah / thee / thay / thee(n)] — plus the past habitual (used to…).

Dialogue: कल तुम कहाँ थे? kal tum kahaan the?

Priya:
जैकब, कल तुम कहाँ थे? फ़ोन पर नहीं थे।
Jacob, kal tum kahaan the? fon par naheen the. [jeh-kub, kuhl tum kuh-hah(n) thay? fohn pur nuh-hee(n) thay]
Jacob, where were you yesterday? You weren't on the phone.
Jacob:
मैं पुरानी दिल्ली में था, अपने दोस्त के साथ।
main puraanee dillee mein thaa, apne dost ke saath. [meh(n) pu-rah-nee dil-lee may(n) thah, up-nay dohst kay sahth]
I was in Old Delhi, with my friend.
Priya:
अच्छा! चाँदनी चौक में? वहाँ भीड़ थी?
achchhaa! chaandnee chauk mein? vahaan bheeR thee? [uch-chhah! chahnd-nee chawk may(n)? vuh-hah(n) bheeR thee]
Oh nice! In Chandni Chowk? Was it crowded there?
Jacob:
हाँ, बहुत भीड़ थी! लोग ही लोग थे।
haan, bahut bheeR thee! log hee log the. [hah(n), bo-hut bheeR thee! lohg hee lohg thay]
Yes, it was very crowded! It was nothing but people. (lit. people-only-people were)
Priya:
और मौसम कैसा था?
aur mausam kaisaa thaa? [awr maw-sum keh-sah thah]
And how was the weather?
Jacob:
दिन में गरमी थी, लेकिन शाम को मौसम ठीक था।
din mein garmee thee, lekin shaam ko mausam Theek thaa. [din may(n) gur-mee thee, lay-kin shahm koh maw-sum Theek thah]
In the daytime it was hot, but in the evening the weather was fine.
Priya:
तुम दोनों वहाँ क्या कर रहे थे?
tum donon vahaan kyaa kar rahe the? [tum doh-noh(n) vuh-hah(n) kyah kur ruh-hay thay]
What were you two doing there?
Jacob:
हम परांठे खा रहे थे — परांठे वाली गली में!
ham paraanThe khaa rahe the — paraanThe vaalee galee mein! [hum puh-rah(n)-Thay khah ruh-hay thay — puh-rah(n)-Thay vah-lee guh-lee may(n)]
We were eating paranthas — in Paranthe Wali Gali!
Priya:
वाह! बचपन में मैं भी वहाँ जाती थी।
vaah! bachpan mein main bhee vahaan jaatee thee. [vah! buhch-pun may(n) meh(n) bhee vuh-hah(n) jah-tee thee]
Wow! In childhood I used to go there too.
Jacob:
सच? जब तुम छोटी थीं, तब तुम कैसी थीं?
sach? jab tum chhoTee theen, tab tum kaisee theen? [such? jub tum chhoh-Tee thee(n), tub tum keh-see thee(n)]
Really? When you were little, what were you like?
Priya:
मैं बहुत शरारती थी! हर रविवार को दादी के साथ बाज़ार जाती थी।
main bahut sharaaratee thee! har ravivaar ko daadee ke saath baazaar jaatee thee. [meh(n) bo-hut shuh-rah-ruh-tee thee! hur ruh-vi-vahr koh dah-dee kay sahth bah-zahr jah-tee thee]
I was very naughty! Every Sunday I used to go to the market with Grandma.
Jacob:
जब मैं छोटा था, मैं हर दिन साइकिल चलाता था।
jab main chhoTaa thaa, main har din saaikil chalaataa thaa. [jub meh(n) chhoh-Tah thah, meh(n) hur din sah-i-kil chuh-lah-tah thah]
When I was little, I used to ride a bicycle every day.
Priya:
और अब?
aur ab? [awr ub]
And now?
Jacob:
अब मैं मेट्रो में बैठता हूँ। ज़िंदगी अलग थी, यार!
ab main meTro mein baiThtaa hoon. zindagee alag thee, yaar! [ub meh(n) may-Troh may(n) behTh-tah hoo(n). zin-duh-gee uh-lug thee, yahr]
Now I sit in the Metro. Life was different, yaar!

परांठे वाली गली paraanThe vaalee galee [puh-rah(n)-Thay vah-lee guh-lee] is a narrow lane off Chandni Chowk where the same families have been frying stuffed paranthas since the 1870s. You eat standing or squeezed onto a bench, and yes — there is always भीड़ bheeR. Going there with Delhi in-laws earns serious points.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
कलkal (m)kuhlyesterday (also: tomorrow — see Lesson 10)
तुम कहाँ थे?tum kahaan the?tum kuh-hah(n) thaywhere were you? (to a man)
भीड़bheeR (f)bheeRcrowd
बहुत भीड़ थीbahut bheeR theebo-hut bheeR theeit was very crowded
मौसमmausam (m)maw-sumweather
मौसम कैसा था?mausam kaisaa thaa?maw-sum keh-sah thahhow was the weather?
गरमीgarmee (f)gur-meeheat, hot weather
बचपन मेंbachpan meinbuhch-pun may(n)in childhood
जब मैं छोटा थाjab main chhoTaa thaajub meh(n) chhoh-Tah thahwhen I was little (man speaking)
जब मैं छोटी थीjab main chhoTee theejub meh(n) chhoh-Tee theewhen I was little (woman speaking)
हर दिनhar dinhur dinevery day
ज़िंदगीzindagee (f)zin-duh-geelife

Past honaa agrees like an adjective: मैं था main thaa (man), मैं थी main thee (woman), तुम थे tum the / तुम थीं tum theen, आप थे / थीं aap the / theen. Even for ONE person, tum and aap take the plural forms the / theen — never तुम था.

Delhiites talk about yesterday half in English: कल फ़ुल भीड़ थी, यार। kal ful bheeR thee, yaar. [kuhl ful bheeR thee, yahr] — "it was FULL crowded yesterday." Doubling is another flavor: लोग ही लोग log hee log "people and only people," गरमी ही गरमी garmee hee garmee "heat, nothing but heat."

Comprehension

Exercise 9A — Answer in Hindi

Answer in full Hindi sentences, using past forms. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 9.

  1. कल जैकब कहाँ था? (kal Jacob kahaan thaa?)
  2. चाँदनी चौक में भीड़ थी या नहीं? (chaandnee chauk mein bheeR thee yaa naheen?)
  3. शाम को मौसम कैसा था? (shaam ko mausam kaisaa thaa?)
  4. जैकब और उसका दोस्त क्या खा रहे थे? (Jacob aur uskaa dost kyaa khaa rahe the?)
  5. बचपन में प्रिया हर रविवार को कहाँ जाती थी? (bachpan mein priyaa har ravivaar ko kahaan jaatee thee?)

Pattern drill: today → yesterday

The move of this lesson: take a present sentence and slide it into the past. है → था/थी/थे; करता हूँ → करता था; कर रहा हूँ → कर रहा था.

Exercise 9B — Put it in the past

Rewrite each sentence in the past. Item 1 is modelled for you: आज गरमी है। → कल गरमी थी। (aaj garmee hai. → kal garmee thee.)

  1. आज बहुत भीड़ है। (aaj bahut bheeR hai.)
  2. मौसम अच्छा है। (mausam achchhaa hai.)
  3. मैं रोज़ चाय पीता हूँ। (main roz chaay peetaa hoon.) — begin with बचपन में
  4. वह दिल्ली में रहती है। (voh dillee mein rehtee hai.)
  5. हम हर दिन क्रिकेट खेलते हैं। (ham har din krikeT khelte hain.)
  6. तुम कहाँ हो? (tum kahaan ho?) — ask about yesterday, to a man
  7. मेरी बहन स्कूल में पढ़ती है। (meree behen skool mein paRhtee hai.)
  8. मैं हिन्दी सीख रहा हूँ। (main hindee seekh rahaa hoon.) — add कल शाम को

Translation practice

Exercise 9C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 9.

  1. Where were you (tum, to a woman) yesterday?
  2. There was a big crowd at the market.
  3. When I was little, I used to play cricket every day. (man speaking)
  4. Yesterday the weather was very good, but there was a lot of heat in the afternoon.

Exercise 9D — Into English

  1. कल शाम को हम घर पर थे। (kal shaam ko ham ghar par the.)
  2. जब मैं छोटी थी, मैं दादी के साथ रहती थी। (jab main chhoTee thee, main daadee ke saath rehtee thee.)
  3. मेरी माँ बहुत अच्छा खाना बनाती थीं। (meree maan bahut achchhaa khaanaa banaatee theen.)
  4. पुरानी दिल्ली में लोग ही लोग थे। (puraanee dillee mein log hee log the.)

Roleplay: last Sunday, minute by minute. Sit with your partner in the evening. You ask: कल तुम कहाँ थीं? मौसम कैसा था? तुम क्या कर रही थीं? (kal tum kahaan theen? mausam kaisaa thaa? tum kyaa kar rahee theen?) She answers, then grills you back with the / kar rahe the forms. Round two: each of you gives two जब मैं छोटा था… / जब मैं छोटी थी… childhood sentences with the past habitual (…kartaa thaa / …kartee thee). Bonus: ask her about a grandparent — she must answer with the respectful plural (banaatee theen, rehte the).
chapters.book4-L10:
Lesson 10 Weekend Plans

The scene: Friday night on the sofa. Tomorrow is free, and Jacob and Priya are negotiating: new film at the mall, or picnic at India Gate? Everything here runs on the future tense — करूँगा / करूँगी / करोगे / करेंगे karoongaa / karoongee / karoge / karenge [kuh-roo(n)-gah / kuh-roo(n)-gee / kuh-roh-gay / kuh-ray(n)-gay] — and the lesson ends with the famous कल kal two-way joke.

Dialogue: कल हम क्या करेंगे? kal ham kyaa karenge?

Jacob:
प्रिया, कल हम क्या करेंगे?
priyaa, kal ham kyaa karenge? [pri-yah, kuhl hum kyah kuh-ray(n)-gay]
Priya, what will we do tomorrow?
Priya:
कल? कल तो शनिवार है! क्या प्लान है?
kal? kal to shanivaar hai! kyaa plaan hai? [kuhl? kuhl toh shuh-ni-vahr heh! kyah plahn heh]
Tomorrow? Tomorrow's Saturday! What's the plan?
Jacob:
हम सिनेमा जाएँगे? पीवीआर में एक नई फ़िल्म है।
ham sinemaa jaayenge? peeveeaar mein ek naee film hai. [hum si-nay-mah jah-ay(n)-gay? pee-vee-ahr may(n) ayk nuh-ee film heh]
Shall we go to the cinema? There's a new film at PVR.
Priya:
हम्म… फ़िल्म तो अगले हफ़्ते भी देखेंगे। कल मौसम अच्छा होगा।
hmm… film to agle hafte bhee dekhenge. kal mausam achchhaa hogaa. [hmm… film toh ug-lay huhf-tay bhee day-khay(n)-gay. kuhl maw-sum uch-chhah hoh-gah]
Hmm… we can see a film next week too. Tomorrow the weather will be nice.
Jacob:
तो?
to? [toh]
So?
Priya:
तो हम इंडिया गेट चलेंगे! पिकनिक करेंगे।
to ham inDiyaa geT chalenge! piknik karenge. [toh hum in-Di-yah gayT chuh-lay(n)-gay! pik-nik kuh-ray(n)-gay]
So we'll go to India Gate! We'll have a picnic.
Jacob:
वाह! हम वहाँ क्या खाएँगे?
vaah! ham vahaan kyaa khaayenge? [vah! hum vuh-hah(n) kyah khah-ay(n)-gay]
Nice! What will we eat there?
Priya:
मैं सैंडविच बनाऊँगी, और तुम आइसक्रीम ख़रीदोगे।
main sainDvich banaaoongee, aur tum aaiskreem khareedoge. [meh(n) sehnD-vich buh-nah-oo(n)-gee, awr tum ah-is-kreem khuh-ree-doh-gay]
I'll make sandwiches, and you'll buy the ice cream.
Jacob:
ठीक है। हम कब निकलेंगे?
Theek hai. ham kab niklenge? [Theek heh. hum kub nik-lay(n)-gay]
Okay. When will we head out?
Priya:
सुबह दस बजे निकलेंगे। शाम को वहाँ बहुत भीड़ होगी।
subah das baje niklenge. shaam ko vahaan bahut bheeR hogee. [su-beh duhs buh-jay nik-lay(n)-gay. shahm koh vuh-hah(n) bo-hut bheeR hoh-gee]
We'll leave at ten in the morning. In the evening it'll be really crowded there.
Jacob:
और रवि? वह भी आएगा?
aur ravi? voh bhee aayegaa? [awr ruh-vi? voh bhee ah-ay-gah]
And Ravi? Will he come too?
Priya:
हाँ, वह हमसे इंडिया गेट पर मिलेगा।
haan, voh hamse inDiyaa geT par milegaa. [hah(n), voh hum-say in-Di-yah gayT pur mi-lay-gah]
Yes, he'll meet us at India Gate.
Jacob:
परफ़ेक्ट। तो कल मैं जल्दी उठूँगा।
parfekT. to kal main jaldee uThoongaa. [pur-fekT. toh kuhl meh(n) juhl-dee u-Thoo(n)-gah]
Perfect. So tomorrow I'll get up early.
Priya:
तुम — और जल्दी उठोगे? अच्छा मज़ाक है!
tum — aur jaldee uThoge? achchhaa mazaak hai! [tum — awr juhl-dee u-Thoh-gay? uch-chhah muh-zahk heh]
You — get up early? Good joke!
Jacob:
अरे! वैसे, एक सवाल — "कल" यानी आज से पहले, या आज के बाद?
arre! vaise, ek savaal — "kal" yaanee aaj se pehle, yaa aaj ke baad? [uh-ray! veh-say, ayk suh-vahl — kuhl yah-nee ahj say peh-lay, yah ahj kay bahd]
Hey! By the way, one question — does "kal" mean before today, or after today?
Priya:
दोनों! कल मैं यहाँ थी, और कल भी यहाँ रहूँगी। सिंपल!
donon! kal main yahaan thee, aur kal bhee yahaan rahoongee. simpal! [doh-noh(n)! kuhl meh(n) yuh-hah(n) thee, awr kuhl bhee yuh-hah(n) ruh-hoo(n)-gee. sim-pul]
Both! Yesterday I was here, and tomorrow I'll be here too. Simple!

The कल kal trick: the word means "one day away from today" — the verb tells you which direction. कल मैं वहाँ था kal main vahaan thaa = yesterday; कल मैं वहाँ रहूँगा kal main vahaan rahoongaa = tomorrow. Same with परसों parson [pur-soh(n)] = two days away, either direction.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
कल क्या करोगे?kal kyaa karoge?kuhl kyah kuh-roh-gaywhat will you do tomorrow? (to a man)
क्या प्लान है?kyaa plaan hai?kyah plahn hehwhat's the plan?
हम चलेंगेham chalengehum chuh-lay(n)-gaywe'll go / let's head there
हम मिलेंगेham milengehum mi-lay(n)-gaywe'll meet
हम कब निकलेंगे?ham kab niklenge?hum kub nik-lay(n)-gaywhen will we head out?
अगले हफ़्तेagle hafteug-lay huhf-taynext week
मौसम अच्छा होगाmausam achchhaa hogaamaw-sum uch-chhah hoh-gahthe weather will be nice
बहुत भीड़ होगीbahut bheeR hogeebo-hut bheeR hoh-geeit will be very crowded
जल्दीjaldeejuhl-deeearly; quickly

परसोंparsonpur-soh(n)day after tomorrow / day before yesterday
यानीyaaneeyah-neethat is, meaning…

No hoon / hai in the future! English speakers want to add an auxiliary: मैं जाऊँगा हूँ is wrong — just मैं जाऊँगा main jaaoongaa. And the ending carries gender: a woman says जाऊँगी, करूँगी, मिलूँगी jaaoongee, karoongee, miloongee. Jacob: -gaa. Priya: -gee. Both together: -ge.

India Gate at night is a Delhi institution: families on the lawns, balloon sellers, and the ice-cream carts — everyone's order is a कुल्फ़ी kulfee [kul-fee] or an orange bar. Real Delhi planning talk is half English: संडे को मूवी देखेंगे, फिर डिनर करेंगे। डन? sanDe ko moovee dekhenge, phir Dinar karenge. Dan? [sun-Day koh moo-vee day-khay(n)-gay, fir Di-nur kuh-ray(n)-gay. Dun] — "Movie on Sunday, then dinner. Done?"

Answer in full sentences, future tense where natural. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 10.

Exercise 10B — Today's habit, tomorrow's plan

  3. मैं जल्दी उठता हूँ। (main jaldee uThtaa hoon.) (man speaking)
  4. तुम आइसक्रीम ख़रीदते हो। (tum aaiskreem khareedte ho.) (to a man)
  5. रवि हमसे बाज़ार में मिलता है। (ravi hamse baazaar mein miltaa hai.)
  6. शाम को बहुत भीड़ होती है। (shaam ko bahut bheeR hotee hai.)
  7. हम दस बजे निकलते हैं। (ham das baje nikalte hain.)
  8. वह नई फ़िल्म देखती है। (voh naee film dekhtee hai.)

Write in Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 10.

  1. What will you (tum, to a woman) do tomorrow?
  2. We will meet at India Gate at five o'clock.
  3. Tomorrow the weather will be nice, so we'll have a picnic.
  4. I (man) will get up early and (I) will make chai.

Exercise 10D — Into English

  1. अगले हफ़्ते हम नई फ़िल्म देखेंगे। (agle hafte ham naee film dekhenge.)
  2. कल शाम को इंडिया गेट पर बहुत भीड़ होगी। (kal shaam ko inDiyaa geT par bahut bheeR hogee.)
  3. रवि परसों हमसे मिलेगा। (ravi parson hamse milegaa.)

Roleplay: plan the real weekend. Do this on a Thursday or Friday, for your actual weekend. Jacob opens: कल हम क्या करेंगे? (kal ham kyaa karenge?) Priya proposes one plan, Jacob proposes another, and you bargain until you agree — using at least five different future verbs (chalenge, dekhenge, khaayenge, milenge, niklenge…). Close the deal with a time: हम कितने बजे निकलेंगे? Then test each other on the joke: she says a कल sentence and you shout "yesterday!" or "tomorrow!" based only on the verb.
chapters.book4-L11:
Lesson 11 Auto-Rickshaw Bargaining

The scene: The classic Delhi rite of passage. Jacob steps out of the house in Lajpat Nagar, flags down an auto, and does his first solo fare negotiation — meter, counter-offer, the works. This is imperative country: soft commands with -ओ -o for the driver (चलो, करो), polite -इए -iye forms back at you (बैठिए, दीजिए).

Dialogue: भैया, चलोगे? bhaiyaa, chaloge?

Jacob:
भैया, ख़ान मार्केट चलोगे?
bhaiyaa, khaan maarkeT chaloge? [bheh-yah, khahn mahr-kayT chuh-loh-gay]
Bhaiya, will you go to Khan Market?
Driver:
बैठिए साहब। डेढ़ सौ रुपये।
baiThiye saahab. DeRh sau rupaye. [beh-Thi-yay sah-hub. DayRh saw ru-puh-yay]
Have a seat, sir. One hundred and fifty rupees.
Jacob:
डेढ़ सौ?! भैया, मीटर से चलो।
DeRh sau?! bhaiyaa, meeTar se chalo. [DayRh saw?! bheh-yah, mee-Tur say chuh-loh]
A hundred and fifty?! Bhaiya, go by the meter.
Driver:
मीटर ख़राब है, साहब।
meeTar kharaab hai, saahab. [mee-Tur khuh-rahb heh, sah-hub]
The meter is broken, sir.
Jacob:
वाह! दिल्ली में हर मीटर ख़राब है?
vaah! dillee mein har meeTar kharaab hai? [vah! dil-lee may(n) hur mee-Tur khuh-rahb heh]
Wow! Is every meter in Delhi broken?
Driver:
अच्छा, आप बताइए।
achchhaa, aap bataaiye. [uch-chhah, ahp buh-tah-i-yay]
Fine, you tell (me your price).
Jacob:
अस्सी रुपये।
assee rupaye. [us-see ru-puh-yay]
Eighty rupees.
Driver:
अरे नहीं साहब! सौ दीजिए। पेट्रोल महँगा है।
arre naheen saahab! sau deejiye. peTrol mehngaa hai. [uh-ray nuh-hee(n) sah-hub! saw dee-ji-yay. payT-rohl meh(n)-gah heh]
Oh no, sir! Give a hundred. Petrol is expensive.
Jacob:
थोड़ा कम करो, भैया। नब्बे?
thoRaa kam karo, bhaiyaa. nabbe? [thoh-Rah kum kuh-roh, bheh-yah. nub-bay]
Come down a little, bhaiya. Ninety?
Driver:
चलिए, आपके लिए नब्बे। बैठिए।
chaliye, aapke liye nabbe. baiThiye. [chuh-li-yay, ahp-kay li-yay nub-bay. beh-Thi-yay]
All right, ninety for you. Sit.
Jacob:
ठीक है। और भैया, धीरे चलाना — जल्दी नहीं है।
Theek hai. aur bhaiyaa, dheere chalaanaa — jaldee naheen hai. [Theek heh. awr bheh-yah, dhee-ray chuh-lah-nah — juhl-dee nuh-hee(n) heh]
Okay. And bhaiya, drive slowly — there's no hurry.
Driver:
आप हिन्दी अच्छी बोलते हैं, साहब!
aap hindee achchhee bolte hain, saahab! [ahp hin-dee uch-chhee bohl-tay heh(n), sah-hub]
You speak good Hindi, sir!
Jacob:
शुक्रिया! मेरी वाइफ़ दिल्ली से है।
shukriyaa! meree vaaif dillee se hai. [shuk-ri-yah! may-ree vah-if dil-lee say heh]
Thanks! My wife is from Delhi.
Driver:
फिर तो आप पक्के दिल्ली वाले हैं! बैठिए, बैठिए।
phir to aap pakke dillee vaale hain! baiThiye, baiThiye. [fir toh ahp puk-kay dil-lee vah-lay heh(n). beh-Thi-yay, beh-Thi-yay]
Then you're a proper Delhi-wala! Sit, sit.

Notice the asymmetry: the driver gives Jacob aap-imperatives (बैठिए, बताइए) because Jacob is the customer; Jacob uses friendly tum-imperatives (चलो, करो) softened with भैया bhaiyaa "brother." That combination — firm form + warm word — is exactly the Delhi register for autos, chai stalls and shops. Saying चलिए to a driver isn't wrong, just unusually formal.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
भैया, चलोगे?bhaiyaa, chaloge?bheh-yah, chuh-loh-gaybhaiya, will you go (there)?
मीटर से चलोmeeTar se chalomee-Tur say chuh-lohgo by the meter
मीटर ख़राब हैmeeTar kharaab haimee-Tur khuh-rahb hehthe meter is broken (the eternal excuse)
कितना लोगे?kitnaa loge?kit-nah loh-gayhow much will you take?
थोड़ा कम करोthoRaa kam karothoh-Rah kum kuh-rohlower it a bit

सौ दीजिएsau deejiyesaw dee-ji-yayplease give a hundred

यहाँ रोकोyahaan rokoyuh-hah(n) roh-kohstop here
महँगा / सस्ताmehngaa / sastaameh(n)-gah / suhs-tahexpensive / cheap

The imperative ladder

LevelचलनाकरनादेनाUse with
तू (intimate/risky)चलकरदेsmall kids; can insult adults
तुम (friendly)चलोकरोदोpartner, friends, bhaiyaa-people
आप (polite)चलिएकीजिएदीजिएelders, in-laws, strangers
casual "do it (later)"चलनाकरनादेनाrelaxed requests: धीरे चलाना

Irregulars to memorize: करना → कीजिए keejiye (not करिए), देना → दीजिए deejiye, लेना → लीजिए leejiye, पीना → पीजिए peejiye. And negative commands take मत: यहाँ मत रुको yahaan mat ruko "don't stop here" — naheen is for statements, mat for commands.

Auto survival kit: agree the fare BEFORE you sit, or insist मीटर से. At stations use the prepaid booth (प्रीपेड preepeD [pree-payD]). Keep ख़ुले पैसे — drivers never have change for a 500. And the magic walk-away: say रहने दो, भैया rehne do, bhaiyaa [reh-nay doh, bheh-yah] "let it be" and turn around slowly — the price usually drops before your third step.

Bargaining is not rude — it is the expected dance for autos and street markets. Smile, keep it playful, and know the fair price (ask your partner first). But don't haggle where it isn't done: metro fares, malls, and anything with a printed price tag (फ़िक्स रेट fiks reT [fiks rayT]).

Comprehension

Exercise 11A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 11.

  1. जैकब कहाँ जा रहा है? (Jacob kahaan jaa rahaa hai?)
  2. ड्राइवर पहले कितने पैसे माँगता है? (Draaivar pehle kitne paise maangtaa hai?)
  3. ड्राइवर के हिसाब से मीटर कैसा है? (Draaivar ke hisaab se meeTar kaisaa hai?)
  4. आख़िर में वे कितने रुपये पर हाँ करते हैं? (aakhir mein ve kitne rupaye par haan karte hain?)
  5. जैकब की हिन्दी अच्छी क्यों है? (Jacob kee hindee achchhee kyon hai?)

For each verb, write the tum-imperative (for the auto driver) and the aap-imperative (for your father-in-law). Model: बैठना → बैठो / बैठिए.

  2. करना (karnaa — to do)

  8. पीना (peenaa — to drink)

Translation practice

Exercise 11C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 11.

  1. Bhaiya, will you go to Connaught Place? (कनॉट प्लेस kanauT ples)
  2. Go by the meter, bhaiya.
  3. Lower it a little — I will give eighty rupees.
  4. Please sit (aap). Please give a hundred rupees. (two short sentences)

Exercise 11D — Into English

  1. भैया, यहाँ रोको। कितने पैसे? (bhaiyaa, yahaan roko. kitne paise?)
  2. मीटर ख़राब है, आप सौ दीजिए। (meeTar kharaab hai, aap sau deejiye.)
  3. धीरे चलाओ, भैया — जल्दी नहीं है। (dheere chalaao, bhaiyaa — jaldee naheen hai.)

Roleplay: beat the quote. Your partner plays the auto driver — and she should play dirty: quote double, claim मीटर ख़राब है, invoke petrol prices. You must (1) open with भैया, … चलोगे? (2) counter with मीटर से चलो, (3) push twice with थोड़ा कम करो and a number, (4) close with ठीक है, चलो — or walk away with रहने दो. Then swap: she's the passenger, and you invent the excuses. Real test: next auto ride, you do the talking.
chapters.book4-L12:
Lesson 12 Delhi Metro & Directions

The scene: Saturday noon. Jacob is at Karol Bagh metro station, heading to Chandni Chowk to meet Priya for paranthas. Mission: buy a token, find the Blue Line, change at Rajiv Chowk — the interchange where all of Delhi seems to be running at once — and come out of the right gate. Imperatives from Lesson 11 do the work, and every postposition drags its noun into the oblique case.

Dialogue: कौनसी लाइन? kaunsee laain?

Jacob:
नमस्ते। एक टोकन दीजिए — चाँदनी चौक।
namaste. ek Tokan deejiye — chaandnee chauk. [nuh-muhs-tay. ayk Toh-kun dee-ji-yay — chahnd-nee chawk]
Hello. One token please — Chandni Chowk.
Clerk:
तीस रुपये।
tees rupaye. [tees ru-puh-yay]
Thirty rupees.
Jacob:
यह लीजिए। कौनसी लाइन जाती है?
yeh leejiye. kaunsee laain jaatee hai? [yeh lee-ji-yeh. kawn-see lah-in jah-tee heh]
Here you go. Which line goes (there)?
Clerk:
ब्लू लाइन लो। राजीव चौक पर उतरो, वहाँ लाइन बदलो — येलो लाइन।
bloo laain lo. raajeev chauk par utro, vahaan laain badlo — yelo laain. [bloo lah-in loh. rah-jeev chawk pur ut-roh, vuh-hah(n) lah-in bud-loh — yay-loh lah-in]
Take the Blue Line. Get off at Rajiv Chowk, change lines there — Yellow Line.
Jacob:
और प्लैटफ़ॉर्म किधर है?
aur plaiTfaurm kidhar hai? [awr plehT-fawrm ki-dhur heh]
And which way is the platform?
Clerk:
सीधा जाओ, फिर बाएँ। सीढ़ियों से नीचे।
seedhaa jaao, phir baayen. seeRhiyon se neeche. [see-dhah jah-oh, fir bah-ay(n). see-Rhi-yoh(n) say nee-chay]
Go straight, then left. Down the stairs.
Jacob (in the train, to an uncle):
अंकल जी, यह ट्रेन राजीव चौक जाती है?
ankal jee, yeh Tren raajeev chauk jaatee hai? [un-kul jee, yeh Trayn rah-jeev chawk jah-tee heh]
Uncle-ji, does this train go to Rajiv Chowk?
Uncle:
हाँ बेटा। राजीव चौक पर उतरो, फिर येलो लाइन लो।
haan beTaa. raajeev chauk par utro, phir yelo laain lo. [hah(n) bay-Tah. rah-jeev chawk pur ut-roh, fir yay-loh lah-in loh]
Yes, son. Get off at Rajiv Chowk, then take the Yellow Line.
Jacob:
वहाँ से चाँदनी चौक कितने स्टेशन हैं?
vahaan se chaandnee chauk kitne sTeshan hain? [vuh-hah(n) say chahnd-nee chawk kit-nay sTay-shun heh(n)]
From there, how many stations is Chandni Chowk?
Uncle:
बस तीन स्टेशन। और बेटा, गेट के पास मत खड़े रहो।
bas teen sTeshan. aur beTaa, geT ke paas mat khaRe raho. [bus teen sTay-shun. awr bay-Tah, gayT kay pahs mut khuh-Ray ruh-hoh]
Just three stations. And son, don't keep standing near the door.
Jacob (on the phone, at Rajiv Chowk):
प्रिया, मैं राजीव चौक पर हूँ। येलो लाइन किधर है? सब लोग जल्दी में हैं!
priyaa, main raajeev chauk par hoon. yelo laain kidhar hai? sab log jaldee mein hain! [pri-yah, meh(n) rah-jeev chawk pur hoo(n). yay-loh lah-in ki-dhur heh? sub lohg juhl-dee may(n) heh(n)]
Priya, I'm at Rajiv Chowk. Which way is the Yellow Line? Everyone's in a hurry!
Priya:
आराम से। साइन देखो — सीधा जाओ, फिर बाएँ। प्लैटफ़ॉर्म नीचे है।
aaraam se. saain dekho — seedhaa jaao, phir baayen. plaiTfaurm neeche hai. [ah-rahm say. sah-in day-khoh — see-dhah jah-oh, fir bah-ay(n). plehT-fawrm nee-chay heh]
Relax. Look at the signs — go straight, then left. The platform is downstairs.
Jacob:
अच्छा, सीढ़ियों से नीचे… अरे! मैं बाहर हूँ! यह पालिका बाज़ार है!
achchhaa, seeRhiyon se neeche… arre! main baahar hoon! yeh paalikaa baazaar hai! [uch-chhah, see-Rhi-yoh(n) say nee-chay… uh-ray! meh(n) bah-hur hoo(n)! yeh pah-li-kah bah-zahr heh]
Okay, down the stairs… hey! I'm outside! This is Palika Bazar!
Priya:
बाहर?! जैकब, वह एग्ज़िट गेट था! अब नया टोकन लो।
baahar?! Jacob, voh egziT geT thaa! ab nayaa Tokan lo. [bah-hur?! jeh-kub, voh ayg-ziT gayT thah! ub nuh-yah Toh-kun loh]
Outside?! Jacob, that was the exit gate! Now buy a new token.
Jacob:
फिर से तीस रुपये?! यह स्टेशन नहीं, भूल-भुलैया है!
phir se tees rupaye?! yeh sTeshan naheen, bhool-bhulaiyaa hai! [fir say tees ru-puh-yeh?! yeh sTay-shun nuh-hee(n), bhool-bhu-leh-yah heh]
Thirty rupees again?! This isn't a station, it's a maze!
Priya:
हा हा! जल्दी आओ, परांठे ठंडे हो रहे हैं।
haa haa! jaldee aao, paraanThe ThanDe ho rahe hain. [hah hah! juhl-dee ah-oh, puh-rah(n)-Thay Thun-Day hoh ruh-hay heh(n)]
Ha ha! Come quickly, the paranthas are getting cold.

The announcement you'll hear

अगला स्टेशन राजीव चौक है। दरवाज़े बाईं तरफ़ खुलेंगे।
aglaa sTeshan raajeev chauk hai. darvaaze baaeen taraf khulenge. [ug-lah sTay-shun rah-jeev chawk heh. dur-vah-zay bah-ee(n) tuh-ruf khu-lay(n)-gay]
The next station is Rajiv Chowk. Doors will open on the left. (lit. doors left-side will-open)

The first coach of every train (look for the pink signs on the platform) is the ladies coach — women only, and the fine is real. Jacob rides the general coaches; Priya can ride anywhere. Offering your seat to elders is standard manners, and eating in the metro is banned — even chai. Security check and X-ray belt at every entrance: keys and phone in the tray, like a tiny airport.

Delhiites ask directions with किधर kidhar [ki-dhur] "which way?" as often as कहाँ "where": येलो लाइन किधर से? yelo laain kidhar se? And the universal answer, with a vague hand-wave: उधर से, सीधा। udhar se, seedhaa. [u-dhur say, see-dhah] "that way, straight." Rajiv Chowk at 6 p.m. is फ़ुल भूल-भुलैया — hold your bag and follow the signs, not the crowd.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
टोकनTokan (m)Toh-kunmetro token
लाइनlaain (f)lah-inline
कौनसी लाइन?kaunsee laain?kawn-see lah-inwhich line?
लाइन बदलोlaain badlolah-in bud-lohchange lines
राजीव चौक पर उतरोraajeev chauk par utrorah-jeev chawk pur ut-rohget off at Rajiv Chowk
सीधा जाओseedhaa jaaosee-dhah jah-ohgo straight
बाएँ / दाएँbaayen / daayenbah-ay(n) / dah-ay(n)(to the) left / right
किधर?kidhar?ki-dhurwhich way?
सीढ़ियों से नीचेseeRhiyon se neechesee-Rhi-yoh(n) say nee-chaydown the stairs
स्टेशनsTeshan (m)sTay-shunstation
गेट नंबर सातgeT nambar saatgayT num-bur sahtgate number seven

Every postposition flips its noun into the oblique: सीढ़ी → सीढ़ियों से seeRhee → seeRhiyon se, गेट के पास, जल्दी में, बाईं तरफ़. The classic slip is direction words: it's बाएँ मुड़ो baayen muRo "turn left," never बाया मुड़ो. When in doubt before se / par / mein / ke — oblique it.

Comprehension

Exercise 12A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 12.

  1. टोकन कितने का है? (Tokan kitne kaa hai?)
  2. जैकब कहाँ लाइन बदलेगा? (Jacob kahaan laain badlegaa?)
  3. राजीव चौक से चाँदनी चौक कितने स्टेशन हैं? (raajeev chauk se chaandnee chauk kitne sTeshan hain?)
  4. ट्रेन में अंकल जी की सलाह क्या है? (Tren mein ankal jee kee salaah kyaa hai?)
  5. जैकब ग़लती से कहाँ बाहर आता है? (Jacob galtee se kahaan baahar aataa hai?)

Pattern drill: same directions, more respect

Exercise 12B — From तुम to आप

A lost elderly uncle asks YOU the way. Convert each tum-direction into the polite aap form. Model: सीधा जाओ → सीधा जाइए (seedhaa jaaiye).

  1. बाएँ मुड़ो। (baayen muRo.)
  2. राजीव चौक पर उतरो। (raajeev chauk par utro.)
  3. येलो लाइन लो। (yelo laain lo.)
  4. सीढ़ियों से नीचे जाओ। (seeRhiyon se neeche jaao.)
  5. यहाँ लाइन बदलो। (yahaan laain badlo.)
  6. गेट नंबर सात से बाहर आओ। (geT nambar saat se baahar aao.)
  7. साइन देखो। (saain dekho.)
  8. गेट के पास मत खड़े रहो। (geT ke paas mat khaRe raho.)

Translation practice

Exercise 12C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 12.

  1. One token please (aap) — Rajiv Chowk.
  2. Which line goes to Chandni Chowk?
  3. Go straight, then turn right. (tum)
  4. Get off at the next station and change lines. (tum)

Exercise 12D — Into English

  1. अगला स्टेशन चाँदनी चौक है। (aglaa sTeshan chaandnee chauk hai.)
  2. दरवाज़े दाईं तरफ़ खुलेंगे। (darvaaze daaeen taraf khulenge.)
  3. पहला डिब्बा लेडीज़ कोच है। (pehlaa Dibbaa leDeez koch hai.)
  4. बाहर मत जाओ — वह एग्ज़िट गेट है! (baahar mat jaao — voh egziT geT hai!)

Roleplay: the blindfold navigator. (1) Metro counter: she's the clerk, you buy a token to a real station, ask कौनसी लाइन? and get directions. (2) She picks a secret Delhi destination and guides you there line by line — ब्लू लाइन लो… राजीव चौक पर बदलो… सीधा जाओ, फिर दाएँ — while you trace it on the metro map and guess the destination. (3) Swap: you guide her from her parents' house to your favorite cafe, all in imperatives. No English, no pointing!

chapters.book4-L13:
Lesson 13 What Happened?!

The scene: Tuesday evening. Jacob walks in late, hair everywhere, holding a slightly squashed bunch of flowers. Priya has been calling all day. Time to tell the whole disaster, start to finish — and that means Unit 14's simple past. One rule runs the show: go/come/arrive/happen verbs take no ने ne [nay] and follow the subject (मैं उठा, मैं गया main uThaa, main gayaa [meh(n) u-Thah, meh(n) guh-yah]); do-verbs put ne on the doer and follow the object (मैंने चाय पी maine chaay pee [meh(n)-nay chah-ay pee]).

Dialogue: आज मेरा दिन बहुत ख़राब था aaj meraa din bahut kharaab thaa

Priya:
जैकब, क्या हुआ? तुम इतने परेशान क्यों हो?
Jacob, kyaa huaa? tum itne pareshaan kyon ho? [jeh-kub, kyah hu-ah? tum it-nay puh-ray-shahn kyoh(n) hoh]
Jacob, what happened? Why are you so frazzled?
Jacob:
अरे, मत पूछो। आज मेरा दिन बहुत ख़राब था।
arre, mat poochho. aaj meraa din bahut kharaab thaa. [uh-ray, mut poo-chhoh. ahj may-rah din bo-hut khuh-rahb thah]
Oh, don't ask. My day today was really bad.
Priya:
क्यों? क्या हुआ?
kyon? kyaa huaa? [kyoh(n)? kyah hu-ah]
Why? What happened?
Jacob:
सुबह मैं देर से उठा, और जल्दी में मैंने फ़ोन नहीं लिया।
subah main der se uThaa, aur jaldee mein maine fon naheen liyaa. [su-beh meh(n) dayr say u-Thah, awr juhl-dee may(n) meh(n)-nay fohn nuh-hee(n) li-yah]
In the morning I got up late, and in the rush I didn't take my phone.
Priya:
अच्छा! इसलिए तुमने फ़ोन नहीं उठाया — मैंने तीन बार फ़ोन किया!
achchhaa! isliye tumne fon naheen uThaayaa — maine teen baar fon kiyaa! [uch-chhah! is-li-yay tum-nay fohn nuh-hee(n) u-Thah-yah — meh(n)-nay teen bahr fohn ki-yah]
Oh! So that's why you didn't pick up — I called three times!
Jacob:
हाँ, सॉरी। फ़ोन सारा दिन घर पर था। फिर मैंने ऑटो लिया…
haan, soree. fon saaraa din ghar par thaa. phir maine auTo liyaa… [hah(n), saw-ree. fohn sah-rah din ghur pur thah. fir meh(n)-nay aw-Toh li-yah]
Yes, sorry. The phone was at home all day. Then I took an auto…
Priya:
और फिर?
aur phir? [awr fir]
And then?
Jacob:
रास्ते में टायर पंक्चर हुआ! मैं पैदल मेट्रो स्टेशन गया।
raaste mein Taayar pankchar huaa! main paidal meTro sTeshan gayaa. [rahs-tay may(n) Tah-yur punk-chur hu-ah! meh(n) peh-dul may-Troh sTay-shun guh-yah]
On the way the tire got punctured! I went to the metro station on foot.
Priya:
नहीं! और मीटिंग? मीटिंग दस बजे थी न?
naheen! aur meeTing? meeTing das baje thee na? [nuh-hee(n)! awr mee-Ting? mee-Ting duhs buh-jay thee nuh]
No! And the meeting? The meeting was at ten, right?
Jacob:
हाँ… मैं ऑफ़िस देर से पहुँचा। बॉस नाराज़ थे।
haan… main ofis der se pahunchaa. baus naaraaz the. [hah(n)… meh(n) aw-fis dayr say puh-hun-chah. baws nah-rahz thay]
Yes… I reached the office late. The boss was annoyed.
Priya:
बेचारा! फिर लंच में क्या खाया?
bechaaraa! phir lanch mein kyaa khaayaa? [bay-chah-rah! fir lunch may(n) kyah khah-yah]
Poor thing! So what did you eat for lunch?
Jacob:
बस एक समोसा। लेकिन ऑफ़िस के पास मुझे एक पुराना दोस्त मिला!
bas ek samosaa. lekin ofis ke paas mujhe ek puraanaa dost milaa! [bus ayk suh-moh-sah. lay-kin aw-fis kay pahs mu-jhay ayk pu-rah-nah dohst mi-lah]
Just one samosa. But near the office I ran into an old friend!
Priya:
अच्छा! कौन?
achchhaa! kaun? [uch-chhah! kawn]
Really! Who?
Jacob:
कॉलेज का दोस्त, अमित। हमने साथ चाय पी।
kaulej kaa dost, amit. hamne saath chaay pee. [kaw-layj kah dohst, uh-mit. hum-nay sahth chah-ay pee]
A friend from college, Amit. We had chai together.
Priya:
वाह! अच्छा, ये फूल किसके लिए हैं?
vaah! achchhaa, ye phool kiske liye hain? [vah! uch-chhah, yay phool kis-kay li-yay heh(n)]
Wow! So… who are these flowers for?
Jacob:
तुम्हारे लिए — ये मैं बाज़ार से लाया। दिन ख़राब था, शाम अच्छी है!
tumhaare liye — ye main baazaar se laayaa. din kharaab thaa, shaam achchhee hai! [tum-hah-ray li-yay — yay meh(n) bah-zahr say lah-yah. din khuh-rahb thah, shahm uch-chhee heh]
For you — I brought them from the market. Bad day, good evening!

Two quiet stars of this dialogue. लाना laanaa "bring" is Unit 14's rebel — it looks like a do-verb but takes no ne: ये मैं लाया ye main laayaa (a woman says लाई laaee [lah-ee]). And "I met a friend" flips its camera in Hindi: मुझे एक दोस्त मिला mujhe ek dost milaa — the friend is the subject, the verb follows him, and there is no ne anywhere.

Key phrases

कुछ नहीं हुआ।kuchh naheen huaa.kuchh nuh-hee(n) hu-ahnothing happened
मेरा दिन ख़राब थाmeraa din kharaab thaamay-rah din khuh-rahb thahmy day was bad
मैं देर से उठाmain der se uThaameh(n) dayr say u-ThahI got up late (woman: उठी uThee)
मैंने ऑटो लियाmaine auTo liyaameh(n)-nay aw-Toh li-yahI took an auto

हमने साथ चाय पीhamne saath chaay peehum-nay sahth chah-ay peewe had chai together
सारा दिनsaaraa dinsah-rah dinall day
पैदलpaidalpeh-dulon foot
बेचारा!bechaaraa!bay-chah-rahpoor thing! (about a woman: बेचारी bechaaree)

The ne checklist, story-sized

Every past verb in Jacob's day falls into one of two boxes. Check the verb, then check who the ending follows:

No ne — verb follows the subjectne — verb follows the object
मैं उठा main uThaaमैंने ऑटो लिया maine auTo liyaa (auTo m)
मैं गया / पहुँचा main gayaa / pahunchaaमैंने चाय पी maine chaay pee (chaay f)
टायर पंक्चर हुआ Taayar pankchar huaaमैंने फ़ोन किया maine fon kiyaa (fon m)
मुझे दोस्त मिला mujhe dost milaaतुमने क्या खाया? tumne kyaa khaayaa?
मैं फूल लाया main phool laayaa (rebel!)मैंने बिरयानी बनाई maine biryaanee banaaee (biryaanee f)

The two instant giveaways, both banned: *मैंने गया *maine gayaa — going verbs never take ne; say मैं गया। main gayaa. And *मैंने चाय पिया *maine chaay piyaa — with ne the verb ignores you and follows the object: chaay is feminine, so मैंने चाय पी। One more: Jacob says उठा / गया / पहुँचा; Priya would say उठी / गई / पहुँची uThee / gaee / pahunchee [u-Thee / guh-ee / puh-hun-chee].

Delhi narrates disasters with relish. The standard opener you'll hear (and can use): और बताओ, कल क्या किया? aur bataao, kal kyaa kiyaa? [awr buh-tah-oh, kuhl kyah ki-yah] "So tell me, what did you do yesterday?" A day like Jacob's gets summed up as फ़ुल ड्रामा हुआ, यार। ful Draamaa huaa, yaar. [ful Drah-mah hu-ah, yahr] "It was full drama, yaar." And when the story ends well: चलो, जो हुआ सो हुआ। chalo, jo huaa so huaa. [chuh-loh, joh hu-ah soh hu-ah] — "well, what happened, happened."

Comprehension

Exercise 13A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences, past forms. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 13.

  1. आज जैकब का दिन कैसा था? (aaj Jacob kaa din kaisaa thaa?)
  2. जैकब का फ़ोन कहाँ था? (Jacob kaa fon kahaan thaa?)
  3. प्रिया ने कितनी बार फ़ोन किया? (priyaa ne kitnee baar fon kiyaa?)
  4. रास्ते में क्या हुआ? (raaste mein kyaa huaa?)
  5. जैकब बाज़ार से क्या लाया? (Jacob baazaar se kyaa laayaa?)

Pattern drill: every day → yesterday

Exercise 13B — Yesterday, one time only

Rewrite each everyday sentence as a one-time past event with कल kal. First decide: ne or no ne? Model: मैं रोज़ ऑटो लेता हूँ। → कल मैंने ऑटो लिया। (main roz auTo letaa hoon. → kal maine auTo liyaa.)

  1. मैं रोज़ जल्दी उठता हूँ। (main roz jaldee uThtaa hoon.)
  2. मैं रोज़ चाय पीता हूँ। (main roz chaay peetaa hoon.)
  3. वह रोज़ ऑफ़िस जाती है। (voh roz ofis jaatee hai.)
  4. हम रोज़ खाना बनाते हैं। (ham roz khaanaa banaate hain.)
  5. तुम रोज़ समोसे खाते हो। (tum roz samose khaate ho.)
  6. प्रिया रोज़ किताब पढ़ती है। (priyaa roz kitaab paRhtee hai.)
  7. वे लोग रोज़ काम करते हैं। (voh log roz kaam karte hain.)
  8. मैं रोज़ आठ बजे पहुँचता हूँ। (main roz aaTh baje pahunchtaa hoon.)

Translation practice

Exercise 13C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. "I" = Jacob (m). Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 13.

  1. What happened? Is everything okay?
  2. I got up late and (I) took an auto.
  3. I didn't eat anything — just one samosa.
  4. I ran into an old friend near the office.

Exercise 13D — Into English

  1. मैंने तीन बार फ़ोन किया, लेकिन तुमने फ़ोन नहीं उठाया। (maine teen baar fon kiyaa, lekin tumne fon naheen uThaayaa.)
  2. रास्ते में ऑटो का टायर पंक्चर हुआ। (raaste mein auTo kaa Taayar pankchar huaa.)
  3. बॉस नाराज़ थे, लेकिन मैंने सॉरी कहा। (baus naaraaz the, lekin maine soree kahaa.)
  4. ये फूल मैं तुम्हारे लिए लाया। (ye phool main tumhaare liye laayaa.)

Roleplay: the disaster report. Tonight, trade real days in the past tense. She opens with और बताओ, आज क्या किया? — you must give at least five past sentences: two with ne (मैंने … किया / खाया / पी), two without (मैं … गया / पहुँचा, … हुआ), and one मुझे … मिला. She fact-checks your endings, then tells her day and you ask the follow-ups: फिर क्या हुआ? तुमने क्या खाया? कौन मिला? Bonus round: retell your worst-ever travel day, one फ़ुल ड्रामा हुआ allowed.
chapters.book4-L14:
Lesson 14 Dinner at the In-Laws'

The scene: Friday evening, Priya's parents' house in Rajouri Garden — Jacob's first proper dinner there as the family's दामाद daamaad [dah-mahd] (son-in-law). This is the high-stakes politeness arena: aap-forms every single time, compliments to the cook, and the sentence that wins every Delhi mother-in-law's heart: आपने क्या-क्या बनाया? aapne kyaa-kyaa banaayaa? [ahp-nay kyah-kyah buh-nah-yah] Grammar on duty: Unit 14's ne plus Unit 15's perfect tenses (आया था, ख़रीदा था aayaa thaa, khareedaa thaa).

Dialogue: आपने क्या-क्या बनाया? aapne kyaa-kyaa banaayaa?

Saas:
आओ बेटा, आओ! खाना बिल्कुल तैयार है।
aao beTaa, aao! khaanaa bilkul taiyaar hai. [ah-oh bay-Tah, ah-oh! khah-nah bil-kul teh-yahr heh]
Come, son, come! The food is all ready.
Jacob:
नमस्ते मम्मी जी! यह मिठाई आपके लिए है।
namaste mummy jee! yeh miThaaee aapke liye hai. [nuh-muhs-tay mum-mee jee! yeh mi-Thah-ee ahp-kay li-yeh heh]
Namaste, Mummy-ji! These sweets are for you.
Saas:
अरे, इसकी क्या ज़रूरत थी! जीते रहो, बेटा।
arre, iskee kyaa zaroorat thee! jeete raho, beTaa. [uh-ray, is-kee kyah zuh-roo-rut thee! jee-tay ruh-hoh, bay-Tah]
Oh, there was no need for this! Bless you, son. (lit. keep living — the standard blessing)
Sasur:
आओ जैकब, बैठो। और बताओ, काम कैसा चल रहा है?
aao Jacob, baiTho. aur bataao, kaam kaisaa chal rahaa hai? [ah-oh jeh-kub, beh-Thoh. awr buh-tah-oh, kahm keh-sah chul ruh-hah heh]
Come, Jacob, sit. So tell (us), how's work going?
Jacob:
अच्छा चल रहा है, पापा जी। वाह — मम्मी जी, आपने क्या-क्या बनाया?
achchhaa chal rahaa hai, paapaa jee. vaah — mummy jee, aapne kyaa-kyaa banaayaa? [uch-chhah chul ruh-hah heh, pah-pah jee. vah — mum-mee jee, ahp-nay kyah-kyah buh-nah-yah]
It's going well, Papa-ji. Wow — Mummy-ji, what all did you make?
Saas:
कुछ ख़ास नहीं — छोले बनाए, रायता बनाया, और तुम्हारे लिए खीर बनाई।
kuchh khaas naheen — chhole banaae, raaytaa banaayaa, aur tumhaare liye kheer banaaee. [kuchh khahs nuh-hee(n) — chhoh-lay buh-nah-ay, rah-ay-tah buh-nah-yah, awr tum-hah-ray li-yay kheer buh-nah-ee]
Nothing special — (I) made chhole, made raita, and made kheer for you. (banaae m pl · banaayaa m · banaaee f — the verb follows each dish!)
Sasur:
पहले खाना, बेटा। लो, गरम-गरम रोटी लो।
pehle khaanaa, beTaa. lo, garam-garam roTee lo. [peh-lay khah-nah, bay-Tah. loh, guh-rum guh-rum roh-Tee loh]
First, food, son. Here, take a hot-hot roti.
Jacob (eating):
खाना बहुत अच्छा है, मम्मी जी। ऐसे छोले मैंने कभी नहीं खाए!
khaanaa bahut achchhaa hai, mummy jee. aise chhole maine kabhee naheen khaae! [khah-nah bo-hut uch-chhah heh, mum-mee jee. eh-say chhoh-lay meh(n)-nay kuh-bhee nuh-hee(n) khah-ay]
The food is wonderful, Mummy-ji. I've never eaten chhole like these!
Saas:
शुक्रिया, बेटा! थोड़े और लो न।
shukriyaa, beTaa! thoRe aur lo na. [shuk-ri-yah, bay-Tah! thoh-Ray awr loh nuh]
Thank you, son! Do take a little more.
Jacob:
बस, मम्मी जी, बस!… अच्छा ठीक है, थोड़ा और दीजिए।
bas, mummy jee, bas!… achchhaa Theek hai, thoRaa aur deejiye. [bus, mum-mee jee, bus!… uch-chhah Theek heh, thoh-Rah awr dee-ji-yay]
Enough, Mummy-ji, enough!… Okay, fine, please give a little more.
Saas:
यह लो। खीर तो मैंने ख़ास तुम्हारे लिए बनाई!
yeh lo. kheer to maine khaas tumhaare liye banaaee! [yeh loh. kheer toh meh(n)-nay khahs tum-hah-ray li-yeh buh-nah-ee]
Here you go. The kheer I made specially for you!
Jacob:
पापा जी, एक सवाल — आप दिल्ली कब आए थे?
paapaa jee, ek savaal — aap dillee kab aae the? [pah-pah jee, ayk suh-vahl — ahp dil-lee kub ah-ay thay]
Papa-ji, one question — when did you (first) come to Delhi?
Sasur:
मैं 1982 में आया था। तब यह शहर बहुत अलग था।
main 1982 mein aayaa thaa. tab yeh sheher bahut alag thaa. [meh(n) un-nees saw buh-yah-see may(n) ah-yah thah. tub yeh sheh-hur bo-hut uh-lug thah]
I came in 1982. Back then this city was very different.
Saas:
और हमने यह घर 1995 में ख़रीदा था। तब यहाँ इतनी गाड़ियाँ नहीं थीं!
aur hamne yeh ghar 1995 mein khareedaa thaa. tab yahaan itnee gaaRiyaan naheen theen! [awr hum-nay yeh ghur un-nees saw puh-chah-nuh-vay may(n) khuh-ree-dah thah. tub yuh-hah(n) it-nee gah-Ri-yah(n) nuh-hee(n) thee(n)]
And we bought this house in 1995. There weren't so many cars here then!
Jacob (leaving):
खाना बहुत अच्छा था, मम्मी जी। मैं फिर आऊँगा — खीर के लिए!
khaanaa bahut achchhaa thaa, mummy jee. main phir aaoongaa — kheer ke liye! [khah-nah bo-hut uch-chhah thah, mum-mee jee. meh(n) fir ah-oo(n)-gah — kheer kay li-yay]
The food was really good, Mummy-ji. I'll come again — for the kheer!
Saas:
ज़रूर आना, बेटा! यह तुम्हारा भी घर है।
zaroor aanaa, beTaa! yeh tumhaaraa bhee ghar hai. [zuh-roor ah-nah, bay-Tah! yeh tum-hah-rah bhee ghur heh]
Do come, son! This is your home too.

Watch the asymmetry of affection: Jacob gives his in-laws aap + plural verbs every time; they give him tum + बेटा — warm, correct, and exactly how Delhi families talk. And remember: with aap the past participle goes plural even for ONE person — to your sasur, आप कब आए थे? aap kab aae the?; to your saas, feminine plural: आप कब आई थीं? aap kab aaee theen? [ahp kub ah-ee thee(n)]

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
आपने क्या-क्या बनाया?aapne kyaa-kyaa banaayaa?ahp-nay kyah-kyah buh-nah-yahwhat all did you make?
कुछ ख़ास नहींkuchh khaas naheenkuchh khahs nuh-hee(n)nothing special (standard cook's modesty)
खाना बहुत अच्छा थाkhaanaa bahut achchhaa thaakhah-nah bo-hut uch-chhah thahthe food was very good
थोड़ा और दीजिएthoRaa aur deejiyethoh-Rah awr dee-ji-yayplease give a little more
बस, और नहींbas, aur naheenbus, awr nuh-hee(n)enough, no more
मैंने कभी नहीं खायाmaine kabhee naheen khaayaameh(n)-nay kuh-bhee nuh-hee(n) khah-yahI've never eaten (anything like this)
आप कब आए थे?aap kab aae the?ahp kub ah-ay thaywhen did you come? (to a man; woman: आई थीं aaee theen)
जीते रहोjeete rahojee-tay ruh-hohbless you (elder's blessing to younger)
फिर आनाphir aanaafir ah-nahcome again (soft command)
छोलेchhole (m pl)chhoh-laychhole, spiced chickpeas
खीरkheer (f)kheerkheer, rice pudding
रायताraaytaa (m)rah-ay-tahraita, spiced yogurt

The perfect ladder at the dinner table

One participle, three distances — all with the same ne and the same object-agreement (Unit 15):

आपने खीर बनाई। aapne kheer banaaee.you made kheer — plain report
आपने खीर बनाई है! aapne kheer banaaee hai!you've made kheer! — it's here, right now, and I can smell it
आपने तब खीर बनाई थी। aapne tab kheer banaaee thee.you had made kheer back then — that famous Diwali, remember?

Two ne-slips to catch before your in-laws do: *आपने कब आए थे *aapne kab aae the — coming and going NEVER take ne: आप कब आए थे? And *मैंने खीर खाया *maine kheer khaayaa — kheer is feminine, and with ne the verb follows the dish, not you: मैंने खीर खाई। maine kheer khaaee. [meh(n)-nay kheer khah-ee]

Delhi's dinner-table superlatives, all safe to copy: ज़बरदस्त! zabardast! [zuh-bur-dust] "outstanding!", क्या बात है! kyaa baat hai! [kyah baht heh] "amazing!" and the approving यह हुई न बात! yeh huee na baat! [yeh hu-ee nuh baht] "now THAT's the spirit!" Learn the बस-dance too: the first बस बस means "keep serving", the second means "really, slow down", and only the third — plate physically shielded with both hands — means enough. Surrender on round two; it's polite.

The feet moment. On arriving and leaving, many Delhiites bend and touch elders' feet — पैर छूना pair chhoonaa [pehr chhoo-nah] — and the elder answers with a blessing: ख़ुश रहो khush raho [khush ruh-hoh] or जीते रहो jeete raho. As the American damaad you are not strictly expected to — but doing it, even once on a festival, melts hearts on the spot. Follow Priya's lead: if she bends, you bend. Many families will wave you up mid-bow (अरे बस, बस!) — the attempt is what counts.

Comprehension

Exercise 14A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences, with ne where it belongs. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 14.

  1. जैकब मम्मी जी के लिए क्या लाया? (Jacob mummy jee ke liye kyaa laayaa?)
  2. सास ने जैकब के लिए ख़ास क्या बनाया? (saas ne Jacob ke liye khaas kyaa banaayaa?)
  3. ससुर जी दिल्ली कब आए थे? (sasur jee dillee kab aae the?)
  4. उन्होंने घर कब ख़रीदा था? (unhonne ghar kab khareedaa thaa?)
  5. जैकब फिर क्यों आएगा? (Jacob phir kyon aaegaa?)

Pattern drill: the compliment machine

Exercise 14B — Praise every dish

For each food, build the full compliment — verb and adjective both agree with the dish. Model: चाय → आपने चाय बनाई — बहुत अच्छी थी! (aapne chaay banaaee — bahut achchhee thee!)

  1. समोसे (samose, m pl)
  2. खीर (kheer, f)
  3. खाना (khaanaa, m)
  4. रोटियाँ (roTiyaan, f pl)
  5. रायता (raaytaa, m)
  6. छोले (chhole, m pl)
  7. कॉफ़ी (kofee, f)
  8. बिरयानी (biryaanee, f)

Translation practice

Exercise 14C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. Use aap-forms for the in-laws. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 14.

  1. Mummy-ji, what did you make?
  2. The food was very good.
  3. Please give a little more kheer. (careful — kheer is feminine!)
  4. Papa-ji, when did you come to Delhi?

Exercise 14D — Into English

  1. बेटा, थोड़े और छोले लो न! (beTaa, thoRe aur chhole lo na!)
  2. मैंने इतना अच्छा खाना कभी नहीं खाया। (maine itnaa achchhaa khaanaa kabhee naheen khaayaa.)
  3. हमने यह घर 1995 में ख़रीदा था। (hamne yeh ghar 1995 mein khareedaa thaa.)
  4. फिर आना — अगली बार मैं बिरयानी बनाऊँगी। (phir aanaa — aglee baar main biryaanee banaaoongee.)

Roleplay: the dinner dress rehearsal. Your partner plays her own mother (she'll enjoy this too much). You must (1) arrive with something and greet — नमस्ते मम्मी जी, यह आपके लिए है; (2) ask आपने क्या-क्या बनाया? and react to each dish with the right gender (बनाया / बनाई / बनाए); (3) survive the बस-dance: refuse once, accept on the second offer with थोड़ा और दीजिए; (4) ask one past-perfect question about the family — आप दिल्ली कब आए थे / आई थीं?; (5) exit with खाना बहुत अच्छा था and answer फिर आना correctly. Then swap: she's the nervous newcomer, you're the feeder-in-chief.
chapters.book4-L15:
Lesson 15 Shopping in Sarojini Nagar

The scene: Saturday morning at Sarojini Nagar market — racks to the horizon, export-surplus treasure, and prices that are merely suggestions. Jacob needs a kurta; Priya is here to teach him the sport. Today's tools: मुझे यह कुर्ता चाहिए mujhe yeh kurtaa chaahiye [mu-jhay yeh kur-tah chah-hi-yeh] for wanting, sizes and colors from Chapter 9, a first taste of comparison — X से सस्ता X se sastaa [say suhs-tah] "cheaper than X" — and the Lesson 11 bargaining moves, back for round two.

Dialogue: यह वाला कितने का है? yeh vaalaa kitne kaa hai?

Priya:
यह है सरोजिनी नगर! बस एक नियम याद रखो — दाम हमेशा आधा करो।
yeh hai sarojinee nagar! bas ek niyam yaad rakho — daam hameshaa aadhaa karo. [yeh heh suh-roh-ji-nee nuh-gur! bus ayk ni-yum yahd ruh-khoh — dahm huh-may-shah ah-dhah kuh-roh]
This is Sarojini Nagar! Just remember one rule — always halve the price.
Shopkeeper:
आइए सर, आइए! क्या चाहिए? कुर्ते, शर्ट, जीन्स — सब है!
aaiye sar, aaiye! kyaa chaahiye? kurte, sharT, jeens — sab hai! [ah-i-yay sur, ah-i-yay! kyah chah-hi-yay? kur-tay, shurT, jeens — sub heh]
Come, sir, come! What would you like? Kurtas, shirts, jeans — we have everything!
Jacob:
मुझे कुर्ता चाहिए — नीला या सफ़ेद।
mujhe kurtaa chaahiye — neelaa yaa safed. [mu-jhay kur-tah chah-hi-yay — nee-lah yah suh-fayd]
I want a kurta — blue or white.
Shopkeeper:
यह देखिए — प्योर कॉटन! बिल्कुल नया माल।
yeh dekhiye — pyor kauTan! bilkul nayaa maal. [yeh day-khi-yeh — pyohr kaw-Tun! bil-kul nuh-yah mahl]
Look at this — pure cotton! Brand-new stock.
Jacob:
हाँ, यह वाला अच्छा है। कितने का है?
haan, yeh vaalaa achchhaa hai. kitne kaa hai? [hah(n), yeh vah-lah uch-chhah heh. kit-nay kah heh]
Yes, this one is nice. How much is it?
Shopkeeper:
सिर्फ़ छह सौ रुपये, सर।
sirf chheh sau rupaye, sar. [sirf chheh saw ru-puh-yay, sur]
Only six hundred rupees, sir.
Priya:
छह सौ?! भैया, यही कुर्ता लाजपत नगर में तीन सौ का है!
chheh sau?! bhaiyaa, yahee kurtaa laajpat nagar mein teen sau kaa hai! [chheh saw?! bheh-yah, yuh-hee kur-tah lahj-put nuh-gur may(n) teen saw kah heh]
Six hundred?! Bhaiya, this very kurta is three hundred in Lajpat Nagar!
Shopkeeper:
अरे दीदी, क्वालिटी देखिए! अच्छा, आपके लिए पाँच सौ।
arre deedee, kvaaliTee dekhiye! achchhaa, aapke liye paanch sau. [uh-ray dee-dee, kvah-li-Tee day-khi-yay! uch-chhah, ahp-kay li-yay pah(n)ch saw]
Oh didi, look at the quality! Fine — five hundred for you.
Jacob:
एक मिनट — यह थोड़ा टाइट है। बड़ा साइज़ दिखाइए।
ek minaT — yeh thoRaa TaaiT hai. baRaa saaiz dikhaaiye. [ayk mi-nuT — yeh thoh-Rah Tah-iT heh. buh-Rah sah-iz di-khah-i-yeh]
One minute — this one is a bit tight. Please show me a bigger size.
Shopkeeper:
यह लीजिए, सर — लार्ज साइज़। ट्रायल रूम उधर है।
yeh leejiye, sar — laarj saaiz. Traayal room udhar hai. [yeh lee-ji-yeh, sur — lahrj sah-iz. Trah-yul room u-dhur heh]
Here you are, sir — large size. The trial room is over there.
Jacob (from the trial room):
अब ठीक है! प्रिया, कैसा लग रहा है?
ab Theek hai! priyaa, kaisaa lag rahaa hai? [ub Theek heh! pri-yah, keh-sah lug ruh-hah heh]
Now it's right! Priya, how does it look?
Priya:
अच्छा लग रहा है! भैया, तीन सौ पचास — आख़िरी दाम।
achchhaa lag rahaa hai! bhaiyaa, teen sau pachaas — aakhiree daam. [uch-chhah lug ruh-hah heh! bheh-yah, teen saw puh-chahs — ah-khi-ree dahm]
It looks good! Bhaiya, three hundred fifty — final price.
Shopkeeper:
चार सौ, दीदी। इससे कम नहीं।
chaar sau, deedee. isse kam naheen. [chahr saw, dee-dee. is-say kum nuh-hee(n)]
Four hundred, didi. No less than that.
Priya:
रहने दो, भैया। चलो जैकब, अगली दुकान।
rehne do, bhaiyaa. chalo Jacob, aglee dukaan. [reh-nay doh, bheh-yah. chuh-loh jeh-kub, ug-lee du-kahn]
Let it be, bhaiya. Come on, Jacob — next shop.
Shopkeeper:
अरे रुकिए, रुकिए! ठीक है — तीन सौ पचास!
arre rukiye, rukiye! Theek hai — teen sau pachaas! [uh-ray ru-ki-yay, ru-ki-yay! Theek heh — teen saw puh-chahs]
Wait, wait! Fine — three hundred fifty!
Jacob:
यह लो, भैया।… प्रिया, तुमने ढाई सौ रुपये बचाए!
yeh lo, bhaiyaa.… priyaa, tumne Dhaaee sau rupaye bachaae! [yeh loh, bheh-yah.… pri-yah, tum-nay Dhah-ee saw ru-puh-yeh buh-chah-ay]
Here you go, bhaiya.… Priya, you saved two hundred and fifty rupees!

यह वाला yeh vaalaa [yeh vah-lah] "this one" and वह वाला voh vaalaa "that one" — learn them as set phrases for pointing at things. Agreement works like achchhaa: यह वाली कमीज़ yeh vaalee kameez, नीले वाले जूते neele vaale joote. The full story of mighty little vaalaa (chai-vaalaa, Dilli-vaalaa, jaane-vaalaa…) comes in Unit 24 — for now, point and say यह वाला दिखाइए।

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
मुझे यह कुर्ता चाहिएmujhe yeh kurtaa chaahiyemu-jhay yay kur-tah chah-hi-yayI want this kurta
यह वालाyeh vaalaayay vah-lahthis one
कितने का है?kitne kaa hai?kit-nay kah hehhow much is it? (f item: कितने की है? kitne kee hai?)
बड़ा साइज़ दिखाइएbaRaa saaiz dikhaaiyebuh-Rah sah-iz di-khah-i-yayplease show a bigger size
यह थोड़ा टाइट हैyeh thoRaa TaaiT haiyay thoh-Rah Tah-iT hehthis is a bit tight (loose: ढीला Dheelaa)
X से सस्ता / महँगाX se sastaa / mehngaasay suhs-tah / meh(n)-gahcheaper / more expensive than X
आख़िरी दामaakhiree daam (m)ah-khi-ree dahmfinal price
इससे कम नहींisse kam naheenis-say kum nuh-hee(n)no less than this
रहने दोrehne doreh-nay dohlet it be (the walk-away, from Lesson 11)

नया मालnayaa maal (m)nuh-yah mahlnew stock, fresh goods
दाम आधा करोdaam aadhaa karodahm ah-dhah kuh-rohhalve the price (the Sarojini rule)

Comparing, the Hindi way

Hindi has no "-er". Name the loser of the comparison with से se and keep the plain adjective — which still agrees with the winner, the thing you're praising:

यह कुर्ता उस कुर्ते से सस्ता है।yeh kurtaa us kurte se sastaa hai. [yeh kur-tah us kur-tay say suhs-tah heh]This kurta is cheaper than that one. (oblique us kurte before se)
यह दुकान उस दुकान से अच्छी है।yeh dukaan us dukaan se achchhee hai. [yeh du-kahn us du-kahn say uch-chhee heh]This shop is better than that shop. (dukaan f → achchhee)
मेट्रो ऑटो से तेज़ है।meTro auTo se tez hai. [may-Troh aw-Toh say tayz heh]The metro is faster than an auto.

Two agreement traps in one market. First, the price question runs on kaa/kee: यह कुर्ता कितने का है? but यह साड़ी कितने की है? yeh saaRee kitne kee hai? — and plural ये जूते कितने के हैं? ye joote kitne ke hain? Second, se hangs on the LOSER: यह उस से सस्ता है means THIS one wins the cheapness contest. Flip the se and you've flipped your whole argument — mid-bargain, that costs money.

Sarojini survival Hindi: stalls shout सौ-सौ, सब सौ में! sau-sau, sab sau mein! [saw-saw, sub saw may(n)] "everything for a hundred!" A shop with एक दाम ek daam [ayk dahm] or फ़िक्स रेट fiks reT on the wall means no bargaining — save your energy. The seller's English is part of the show — "pyor kauTan, laiTesT fashion, sar!" — and the counter-move is Priya's line: quote another market. लाजपत नगर में तीन सौ का है works even if you've never been to Lajpat Nagar. (We didn't tell you that.)

Sarojini Nagar is Delhi's great equalizer — students, aunties and fashion editors all elbow through the same lanes, because the racks carry export surplus: brands you know, at a tenth of the mall price, sometimes with the original tags. Go on a weekday if you can (weekends are shoulder-to-shoulder), carry small notes, and note the market is closed on Mondays. Checking your haul over chai afterwards is part of the ritual — every purchase must be announced with its price, and the lower the number, the bigger the glory.

Comprehension

Exercise 15A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 15.

  1. जैकब को क्या चाहिए? (Jacob ko kyaa chaahiye?)
  2. दुकानदार पहले कितने पैसे माँगता है? (dukaandaar pehle kitne paise maangtaa hai?)
  3. प्रिया के हिसाब से यही कुर्ता लाजपत नगर में कितने का है? (priyaa ke hisaab se yahee kurtaa laajpat nagar mein kitne kaa hai?)
  4. पहला कुर्ता कैसा है? (pehlaa kurtaa kaisaa hai?)
  5. आख़िर में कुर्ता कितने का मिलता है? (aakhir mein kurtaa kitne kaa miltaa hai?)

Pattern drill: price it, then beat it

Exercise 15B — Ask and compare

Items 1–4: ask the price with the right form of kaa/kee/ke. Model: कुर्ता → यह कुर्ता कितने का है? Items 5–8: build the comparison from the cue. Model: [यह कुर्ता · वह कुर्ता · सस्ता] → यह कुर्ता उस कुर्ते से सस्ता है।

  1. साड़ी (saaRee, f)
  2. जूते (joote, m pl)
  3. टी-शर्ट (Tee-sharT, f)
  4. स्वेटर (sveTar, m)
  5. [मेट्रो · ऑटो · तेज़] (meTro · auTo · tez)
  6. [यह दुकान · वह दुकान · अच्छा] (yeh dukaan · voh dukaan · achchhaa)
  7. [दिल्ली · न्यूयॉर्क · पुराना] (dillee · nyooyaurk · puraanaa)
  8. [यह कमीज़ · वह कमीज़ · महँगा] (yeh kameez · voh kameez · mehngaa)

Translation practice

Exercise 15C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 15.

  1. I want this kurta. How much is it?
  2. This is very expensive — please show a cheap one. (aap)
  3. This shirt is a little tight. Please show a big size. (कमीज़ is feminine!)
  4. Chai is cheaper than coffee.

Exercise 15D — Into English

  1. कौनसा रंग चाहिए — नीला या काला? (kaunsaa rang chaahiye — neelaa yaa kaalaa?)
  2. यह वाला कितने का है? (yeh vaalaa kitne kaa hai?)
  3. यह दुकान उस दुकान से महँगी है। (yeh dukaan us dukaan se mehngee hai.)
  4. रहने दो भैया — चार सौ बहुत ज़्यादा है। (rehne do bhaiyaa — chaar sau bahut zyaadaa hai.)

Roleplay: the closet shop. Lay five clothes from your own closet on the bed — that's the shop, and your partner is its ruthless dukaandaar. For each item you must: (1) ask the price with the right कितने का / की / के, (2) gasp and counter at half, (3) fire one comparison — यह उस वाले से अच्छा है? लाजपत नगर में सस्ता है! — and (4) close with ठीक है, दे दो or walk away with रहने दो. She sets secret floor prices in advance; count who wins more rounds. Then swap roles — and next Saturday, do it for real in Sarojini. Budget: 500 rupees, minimum three items, full report in Hindi over chai.
chapters.book4-L16:
Lesson 16 Not Feeling Well

The scene: Monday morning. Jacob surfaces from the blanket looking grey — yesterday's monsoon soaking has caught up with him. One trip to the neighbourhood clinic, one very determined Priya, and one glass of turmeric milk later, he'll be fine. The grammar here is Chapter 8's body-talk in action: feelings land ON you with को ko and लगना lagnaa [lug-nah] (मुझे ठंड लग रही है mujhe ThanD lag rahee hai), and Unit 17's obligation frame tells you what to do about it (मुझे आराम करना चाहिए mujhe aaraam karnaa chaahiye).

Dialogue: तबियत ठीक नहीं है tabiyat Theek naheen hai

Priya:
जैकब, उठो! नौ बजे हैं।
Jacob, uTho! nau baje hain. [jeh-kub, u-Thoh! naw buh-jay heh(n)]
Jacob, get up! It's nine o'clock.
Jacob:
प्रिया… तबियत ठीक नहीं है। सिर में दर्द है, और ठंड लग रही है।
priyaa… tabiyat Theek naheen hai. sir mein dard hai, aur ThanD lag rahee hai. [pri-yah… tuh-bi-yut Theek nuh-hee(n) heh. sir may(n) durd heh, awr ThunD lug ruh-hee heh]
Priya… I'm not feeling well. My head aches, and I'm feeling cold.
Priya (feeling his forehead):
अरे, बुखार है! कल बारिश में भीगे थे न? चलो, डॉक्टर के पास।
arre, bukhaar hai! kal baarish mein bheege the na? chalo, DaukTar ke paas. [uh-ray, bu-khahr heh! kuhl bah-rish may(n) bhee-gay thay nuh? chuh-loh, Dawk-Tur kay pahs]
Oh no, you have a fever! You got soaked in the rain yesterday, didn't you? Come on — to the doctor.
Jacob:
ज़रूरत नहीं है, मैं ठीक—
zaroorat naheen hai, main Theek— [zuh-roo-rut nuh-hee(n) heh, meh(n) Theek]
There's no need, I'm fi—
Priya:
जैकब। चलो। अभी।
Jacob. chalo. abhee. [jeh-kub. chuh-loh. uh-bhee]
Jacob. Come. Now.
Doctor (at the clinic):
आइए, बैठिए। बताइए, क्या हुआ?
aaiye, baiThiye. bataaiye, kyaa huaa? [ah-i-yay, beh-Thi-yay. buh-tah-i-yay, kyah hu-ah]
Come in, have a seat. Tell me — what happened?
Jacob:
डॉक्टर साहब, तबियत ठीक नहीं है। बुखार है और सिर में दर्द है।
DaukTar saahab, tabiyat Theek naheen hai. bukhaar hai aur sir mein dard hai. [Dawk-Tur sah-hub, tuh-bi-yut Theek nuh-hee(n) heh. bu-khahr heh awr sir may(n) durd heh]
Doctor sahab, I'm not feeling well. I have a fever and a headache.
Doctor:
कब से?
kab se? [kub say]
Since when?
Jacob:
कल रात से। गला भी ख़राब है।
kal raat se. galaa bhee kharaab hai. [kuhl raht say. guh-lah bhee khuh-rahb heh]
Since last night. My throat is bad too.
Doctor:
मुँह खोलिए… हाँ, गला लाल है। ठंड लग गई है — कोई बड़ी बात नहीं।
munh kholiye… haan, galaa laal hai. ThanD lag gaee hai — koee baRee baat naheen. [mu(n)h khoh-li-yay… hah(n), guh-lah lahl heh. ThunD lug guh-ee heh — koh-ee buh-Ree baht nuh-hee(n)]
Open your mouth… yes, the throat is red. You've caught a chill — nothing serious.
Doctor:
यह दवाई लीजिए — दिन में दो बार, खाने के बाद। और आराम कीजिए।
yeh davaaee leejiye — din mein do baar, khaane ke baad. aur aaraam keejiye. [yeh duh-vah-ee lee-ji-yeh — din may(n) doh bahr, khah-nay kay bahd. awr ah-rahm kee-ji-yeh]
Take this medicine — twice a day, after food. And rest.
Priya (back home):
तुमने दवाई ली? अब यह लो — हल्दी वाला दूध!
tumne davaaee lee? ab yeh lo — haldee vaalaa doodh! [tum-nay duh-vah-ee lee? ub yeh loh — hul-dee vah-lah doodh]
Did you take the medicine? Now take this — turmeric milk!
Jacob:
यह क्या है?! मुझे हल्दी वाला दूध नहीं पीना!
yeh kyaa hai?! mujhe haldee vaalaa doodh naheen peenaa! [yeh kyah heh?! mu-jhay hul-dee vah-lah doodh nuh-hee(n) pee-nah]
What is this?! I don't want to drink turmeric milk!
Priya:
पीना पड़ेगा! घरेलू नुस्ख़ा है — मम्मी की स्पेशल रेसिपी।
peenaa paRegaa! ghareloo nuskhaa hai — mummy kee speshal resipee. [pee-nah puh-Ray-gah! ghuh-ray-loo nus-khah heh — mum-mee kee spay-shul ray-si-pee]
You'll have to drink it! It's a home remedy — Mummy's special recipe.
Jacob (drinking):
हम्म… अरे! यह तो अच्छा है!
hmm… arre! yeh to achchhaa hai! [hmm… uh-ray! yeh toh uch-chhah heh]
Hmm… hey! This is actually good!
Priya:
मैंने बताया था न! अब आराम करो — कल तक सब ठीक होगा।
maine bataayaa thaa na! ab aaraam karo — kal tak sab Theek hogaa. [meh(n)-nay buh-tah-yah thah nuh! ub ah-rahm kuh-roh — kuhl tuk sub Theek hoh-gah]
I told you so! Now rest — by tomorrow everything will be fine.

ठंड लग गई है ThanD lag gaee hai [ThunD lug guh-ee heh] "(I've) caught a chill" — learn this as a set phrase; every Delhi doctor and every aunty says it exactly this way. (The two-verb trick inside it, lag + gaee, is Unit 19's grammar — for now it's simply what one says.) Compare plain ठंड लग रही है "I'm feeling cold right now" — feeling versus caught.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
तबियत ठीक नहीं हैtabiyat Theek naheen hai (tabiyat f)tuh-bi-yut Theek nuh-hee(n) heh(I'm) not feeling well
सिर में दर्द हैsir mein dard haisir may(n) durd heh(my) head aches
मुझे बुखार हैmujhe bukhaar hai (bukhaar m)mu-jhay bu-khahr hehI have a fever
गला ख़राब हैgalaa kharaab hai (galaa m)guh-lah khuh-rahb heh(my) throat is bad / sore
ठंड लग गई हैThanD lag gaee haiThunD lug guh-ee heh(I've) caught a chill (set phrase)
कब से?kab se?kub saysince when?
कल रात सेkal raat sekuhl raht saysince last night
यह दवाई लीजिएyeh davaaee leejiye (davaaee f)yay duh-vah-ee lee-ji-yayplease take this medicine
दिन में दो बारdin mein do baardin may(n) doh bahrtwice a day
आराम करो / कीजिएaaraam karo / keejiyeah-rahm kuh-roh / kee-ji-yayrest (tum / aap)
