How the body complains — and what to do about it

Ailments land on you (Unit 10's ko-frame); duties land on you the same way (Unit 17). Two halves of one visit to the doctor:

The complaintThe prescription
मुझे बुखार है। mujhe bukhaar hai.मुझे आराम करना चाहिए। mujhe aaraam karnaa chaahiye. — should
मुझे ठंड लग रही है। mujhe ThanD lag rahee hai.मुझे दवाई लेनी है। mujhe davaaee lenee hai. — have to (davaaee f → lenee!)
मुझे खाँसी है। mujhe khaansee hai. [khah(n)-see]मुझे घर पर रहना पड़ेगा। mujhe ghar par rehnaa paRegaa. — no choice
मुझे चक्कर आ रहा है। mujhe chakkar aa rahaa hai. [chuk-kur]मुझे पानी पीना चाहिए। mujhe paanee peenaa chaahiye.

Never *मैं बुखार हूँ *main bukhaar hoon — that announces "I AM a fever." Illness happens TO you: मुझे बुखार है। Same logic as pasand and chaahiye from Unit 10. And in obligation sentences the infinitive watches the object: davaaee is feminine, so मुझे दवाई लेनी चाहिए mujhe davaaee lenee chaahiye — never *लेना चाहिए when the thing you're taking is feminine.

Street-Delhi symptom talk: सर फट रहा है, यार। sar phaT rahaa hai, yaar. [sur phuT ruh-hah heh, yahr] "my head is splitting" (Delhi says sar as often as sir), and बुखार हो गया bukhaar ho gayaa [bu-khahr hoh guh-yah] "came down with a fever" — another Unit 19 two-verb phrase to recognize now. The chemist (केमिस्ट kemisT [kay-misT]) on every corner will happily sell you a strip of paracetamol and a diagnosis; for anything real, go where Priya takes you.

Refusing the हल्दी वाला दूध is not an available move. Home remedies — घरेलू नुस्ख़े ghareloo nuskhe [ghuh-ray-loo nus-khay] — are how Indian households love a sick person: turmeric milk for everything, ginger chai (अदरक वाली चाय adrak vaalee chaay [ud-ruk vah-lee chah-ay]) for the throat, and in winter the bitter herbal काढ़ा kaaRhaa [kah-Rhah]. Your sneeze will reach your saas before it reaches the doctor, and a thermos may follow. Drink it, say अब बेहतर है ab behtar hai [ub beh-tur heh] "it's better now" — and mean it, because oddly enough it works.

Comprehension

Exercise 16A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 16.

  1. जैकब की तबियत कैसी है? (Jacob kee tabiyat kaisee hai?)
  2. जैकब को कब से बुखार है? (Jacob ko kab se bukhaar hai?)
  3. डॉक्टर के हिसाब से क्या हुआ है? (DaukTar ke hisaab se kyaa huaa hai?)
  4. जैकब को दिन में कितनी बार दवाई लेनी है? (Jacob ko din mein kitnee baar davaaee lenee hai?)
  5. प्रिया जैकब के लिए क्या लाती है? (priyaa Jacob ke liye kyaa laatee hai?)

Pattern drill: complain, then obey

Exercise 16B — The clinic two-step

Items 1–4: turn the word into a full complaint (mujhe…). Model: बुखार → मुझे बुखार है। Items 5–8: turn the cue into an obligation sentence — watch the infinitive's agreement. Model: [आराम करना + चाहिए] → मुझे आराम करना चाहिए।

  1. ठंड (ThanD — right now!)
  2. सिर + दर्द (sir + dard)
  3. खाँसी (khaansee)
  4. चक्कर (chakkar — right now!)
  5. [दवाई लेना + चाहिए] (davaaee lenaa + chaahiye)
  6. [गरम पानी पीना + है] (garam paanee peenaa + hai)
  7. [घर पर रहना + पड़ेगा] (ghar par rehnaa + paRegaa)
  8. [आज आराम करना + चाहिए] (aaj aaraam karnaa + chaahiye — about your partner: उसे use)

Translation practice

Exercise 16C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 16.

  1. I'm not feeling well — I have a headache.
  2. I've had a fever since last night. (mujhe… se…)
  3. Please take this medicine twice a day. (aap)
  4. You (tum) should rest today.

Exercise 16D — Into English

  1. क्या हुआ? कब से तबियत ख़राब है? (kyaa huaa? kab se tabiyat kharaab hai?)
  2. ठंड लग गई है — कोई बड़ी बात नहीं। (ThanD lag gaee hai — koee baRee baat naheen.)
  3. मुझे हल्दी वाला दूध पीना पड़ेगा। (mujhe haldee vaalaa doodh peenaa paRegaa.)
  4. गरम पानी पीजिए और आराम कीजिए। (garam paanee peejiye aur aaraam keejiye.)

Roleplay: doctor-doctor. Round one: she's the doctor, you're the patient with three symptoms of your choosing. She must ask क्या हुआ? कब से? and you must answer with full mujhe-sentences plus a time (कल रात से, दो दिन से). She prescribes with aap-imperatives — दवाई लीजिए, आराम कीजिए — and you convert each order into your own obligation sentence: ठीक है, मुझे दवाई लेनी चाहिए। Round two: swap — and she is not allowed to laugh at your मुँह खोलिए. Round three: she offers the हल्दी वाला दूध; your only escape phrase is a perfect पीना पड़ेगा, मुझे पता है।

chapters.book4-L17:
Lesson 17 Can You Help Me?

The scene: Saturday afternoon. Jacob is on a secret solo mission in Old Delhi — jalebis from the famous shop near Chandni Chowk, a surprise for Priya. But the lanes of Old Delhi eat GPS signals and tourists alike, his phone is dead, and every alley looks the same. Time to deploy the most useful sentence in the whole language: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं? kyaa aap meree madad kar sakte hain? [kyah ahp may-ree muh-dud kur suk-tay heh(n)] This is saknaa country — "can, be able" — with its shy cousin paanaa "manage to" for graceful apologies.

Dialogue, part one: lost in the lanes

Jacob:
माफ़ कीजिए, अंकल जी… क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?
maaf keejiye, uncle jee… kyaa aap meree madad kar sakte hain? [mahf kee-ji-yay, un-kul jee… kyah ahp may-ree muh-dud kur suk-tay heh(n)]
Excuse me, uncle-ji… can you help me?
Uncle:
हाँ-हाँ, बिल्कुल। बताइए, बेटा।
haan-haan, bilkul. bataaiye, beTaa. [hah(n)-hah(n), bil-kul. buh-tah-i-yay, bay-Tah]
Yes, yes, of course. Tell me, son.
Jacob:
मुझे रास्ता नहीं पता, और मेरा फ़ोन भी बंद है।
मैं चाँदनी चौक मेट्रो स्टेशन जाना चाहता हूँ।
mujhe raastaa naheen pataa, aur meraa fon bhee band hai. main chaandnee chauk meTro sTeshan jaanaa chaahtaa hoon. [mu-jhay rahs-tah nuh-hee(n) puh-tah, awr may-rah fohn bhee bund heh. meh(n) chah(n)d-nee chawk may-Troh sTay-shun jah-nah chah-tah hoo(n)]
I don't know the way, and my phone is dead too. I want to go to Chandni Chowk metro station. (band = "closed" — Delhi's word for a dead phone)
Uncle:
कोई बात नहीं। सीधा जाइए, फिर बाएँ मुड़िए। बस पाँच मिनट का रास्ता है।
koee baat naheen. seedhaa jaaiye, phir baayen muRiye. bas paanch minaT kaa raastaa hai. [koh-ee baht nuh-hee(n). see-dhah jah-i-yay, fir bah-ay(n) mu-Ri-yay. bus pah(n)ch mi-nuT kah rahs-tah heh]
No problem. Go straight, then turn left. It's just five minutes away.
Jacob:
माफ़ कीजिए… मैं समझ नहीं पाया। क्या आप थोड़ा धीरे बोल सकते हैं?
maaf keejiye… main samajh naheen paayaa. kyaa aap thoRaa dheere bol sakte hain? [mahf kee-ji-yay… meh(n) suh-mujh nuh-hee(n) pah-yah. kyah ahp thoh-Rah dhee-ray bohl suk-tay heh(n)]
Sorry… I didn't quite catch that. Can you speak a little slowly?
Uncle:
(धीरे-धीरे) सीधा — फिर — बाएँ। ठीक है?
और सुनिए — अगली गली में मशहूर जलेबी वाला है।
ख़ाली हाथ मत जाइए!
(dheere-dheere) seedhaa — phir — baayen. Theek hai? aur suniye — aglee galee mein mashhoor jalebee vaalaa hai. khaalee haath mat jaaiye! [see-dhah — fir — bah-ay(n). Theek heh? awr su-ni-yay — ug-lee guh-lee may(n) muhsh-hoor juh-lay-bee vah-lah heh. khah-lee hahth mut jah-i-yay]
(Slowly) Straight — then — left. Okay? And listen — the famous jalebi shop is in the next lane. Don't go home empty-handed!
Jacob:
जी, अब समझा! और जलेबी… मैं वहीं तो जा रहा हूँ! आपने मेरी बहुत मदद की।
jee, ab samjhaa! aur jalebee… main vaheen to jaa rahaa hoon! aapne meree bahut madad kee. [jee, ub sum-jhah! awr juh-lay-bee… meh(n) vuh-hee(n) toh jah ruh-hah hoo(n)! ahp-nay may-ree buh-hut muh-dud kee]
Yes, now I've got it! And jalebis… that's exactly where I'm going! You've helped me a lot.
Uncle:
अरे वाह! आप तो अच्छी हिन्दी बोलते हैं!
arre vaah! aap to achchhee hindee bolte hain! [uh-ray vah! ahp toh uch-chhee hin-dee bohl-tay heh(n)]
Oh wow! You speak good Hindi!
Jacob:
मैं हिन्दी बोल सकता हूँ — थोड़ी-थोड़ी!
main hindee bol saktaa hoon — thoRee-thoRee! [meh(n) hin-dee bohl suk-tah hoo(n) — thoh-Ree thoh-Ree]
I can speak Hindi — a little-little! (hindee is feminine, so thoRee — his very first line from Lesson 1, upgraded with saknaa)

Dialogue, part two: the tables turn

That evening, outside the flat in Lajpat Nagar. The neighbor aunty is at the bottom of the stairs with shopping bags.

Aunty:
जैकब बेटा! ज़रा सुनो! क्या तुम मेरी मदद कर सकते हो?
Jacob beTaa! zaraa suno! kyaa tum meree madad kar sakte ho? [jay-kub bay-Tah! zuh-rah su-noh! kyah tum may-ree muh-dud kur suk-tay hoh]
Jacob, son! Listen a moment! Can you help me? (elders use tum downward — that's affection, not rudeness)
Jacob:
जी आंटी जी, बिल्कुल! बताइए।
jee aunty jee, bilkul! bataaiye. [jee ahn-Tee jee, bil-kul! buh-tah-i-yay]
Yes aunty-ji, of course! Tell me.
Aunty:
यह थैला बहुत भारी है, और मैं सीढ़ियाँ नहीं चढ़ सकती।
yeh thailaa bahut bhaaree hai, aur main seeRhiyaan naheen chaRh saktee. [yeh theh-lah buh-hut bhah-ree heh, awr meh(n) see-Rhi-yah(n) nuh-hee(n) chuRh suk-tee]
This bag is very heavy, and I can't climb the stairs. (saktee — saknaa agrees with her, feminine)
Jacob:
कोई बात नहीं। लाइए, थैला मुझे दीजिए।
koee baat naheen. laaiye, thailaa mujhe deejiye. [koh-ee baht nuh-hee(n). lah-i-yay, theh-lah mu-jhay dee-ji-yay]
No problem. Here, give me the bag. (laaiye = "bring (it)" — the hand-it-over word)
Aunty:
जीते रहो, बेटा! छह महीने पहले तुम "नमस्ते" भी
नहीं बोल पाते थे — और आज हिन्दी में मेरी मदद कर रहे हो!
jeete raho, beTaa! chheh maheene pehle tum "namaste" bhee naheen bol paate the — aur aaj hindee mein meree madad kar rahe ho! [jee-tay ruh-hoh, bay-Tah! chheh muh-hee-nay peh-lay tum nuh-muhs-tay bhee nuh-hee(n) bohl pah-tay thay — awr ahj hin-dee may(n) may-ree muh-dud kur ruh-hay hoh]
Long may you live, son! Six months ago you couldn't even manage a "namaste" — and today you're helping me, in Hindi!
Jacob:
धीरे-धीरे, आंटी जी… थोड़ा-थोड़ा, हर दिन।
dheere-dheere, aunty jee… thoRaa-thoRaa, har din. [dhee-ray dhee-ray, ahn-Tee jee… thoh-Rah thoh-Rah, hur din]
Slowly-slowly, aunty-ji… a little-little, every day.

Meet the request ladder. Bottom rung, Lesson 11 style: बताओ / बताइए bataao / bataaiye — a command, fine for autos and shops. Top rung, this lesson: क्या आप बता सकते हैं? kyaa aap bataa sakte hain? [kyah ahp buh-tah suk-tay heh(n)] "could you tell me?" — a question about ability, which is exactly how English softens requests too. Use the ladder's top with strangers you're asking favors of, and note where naheen likes to sit: inside the verb cluster — समझ नहीं पाया, चढ़ नहीं सकती (also fine: नहीं चढ़ सकती).

Key phrases

The can-do kit

Jobहिन्दीRomanNotes
I can (m / f)मैं बोल सकता / सकती हूँmain bol saktaa / saktee hoonstem + saknaa, agrees with subject

couldn't (past)मैं नहीं सो सकाmain naheen so sakaapast saknaa — almost always negative

The Unit 16 iron rule rides again: never ने with सकना, पाना, चुकना — even when the main verb is a ne-verb. In the dialogue both patterns sit side by side: आपने मेरी मदद की aapne meree madad kee (plain past of karnaa → ne) but मैं समझ नहीं पाया main samajh naheen paayaa — no ne, and the helper agrees with main. Writing ✗ मैंने समझ नहीं पाया is the classic slip; one glance at the helper verb saves you.

Direction-asking, Delhi rules: (1) Nobody ever says "I don't know" — you will receive directions, confident ones, possibly fictional. Ask two or three people and average. (2) सीधा seedhaa plus a loose forward hand-flick can mean anything from 50 meters to Gurgaon. (3) बस पाँच मिनट bas paanch minaT is a unit of encouragement, not of time. (4) The magic word is ज़रा zaraa: ज़रा सुनिए zaraa suniye [zuh-rah su-ni-yay] "excuse me a sec" — it makes any request feather-light. And pick your address word: bhaiyaa for the shop, uncle jee / aunty jee for anyone your parents' age.

In a Delhi neighborhood, helping isn't a favor — it's membership. Carrying an aunty's bags, reaching the top shelf, pushing a stalled scooter: refuse none of these. Payment arrives instantly as blessings: जीते रहो jeete raho [jee-tay ruh-hoh] "long may you live," ख़ुश रहो khush raho [khush ruh-hoh] "stay happy." The day the aunties start asking you for help — as one just did — you are officially part of the building.

Comprehension

Exercise 17A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 17.

  1. जैकब को क्या नहीं पता? (Jacob ko kyaa naheen pataa?)
  2. जैकब का फ़ोन कैसा है? (Jacob kaa fon kaisaa hai?)
  3. मेट्रो स्टेशन कितने मिनट का रास्ता है? (meTro sTeshan kitne minaT kaa raastaa hai?)
  4. अगली गली में क्या है? (aglee galee mein kyaa hai?)
  5. आंटी जी क्या नहीं चढ़ सकतीं? (aunty jee kyaa naheen chaRh sakteen?)

Pattern drill: ask it softly, decline it gracefully

Exercise 17B — Requests and apologies

Items 1–4: turn the command into a polite question with क्या आप … सकते हैं? (kyaa aap … sakte hain?). Items 5–8: turn "didn't" into "couldn't manage" with paanaa — and watch ne disappear. Model: मैंने खाना नहीं बनाया → मैं खाना नहीं बना पाया।

  1. धीरे बोलिए। (dheere boliye.)
  2. रास्ता बताइए। (raastaa bataaiye.)
  3. यहाँ रुकिए। (yahaan rukiye.)
  4. थैला उठाइए। (thailaa uThaaiye.) (uThaanaa = to lift)
  5. मैं कल नहीं आया। (main kal naheen aayaa.)
  6. मैं रात को नहीं सोया। (main raat ko naheen soyaa.)
  7. मैंने जवाब नहीं दिया। (maine javaab naheen diyaa.)
  8. मैंने खाना नहीं खाया। (maine khaanaa naheen khaayaa.)

Translation practice

Exercise 17C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. You are Jacob (m). Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 17.

  1. Excuse me — can you (aap, m) help me?
  2. I don't know the way. My phone is dead.
  3. Can you speak slowly? I didn't catch that. (use paanaa)
  4. May I ask you a question?

Exercise 17D — Into English

  1. मैं सीढ़ियाँ नहीं चढ़ सकती — थैला बहुत भारी है। (main seeRhiyaan naheen chaRh saktee — thailaa bahut bhaaree hai.)
  2. कल रात मैं सो नहीं पाया। (kal raat main so naheen paayaa.)
  3. क्या आप मेरे लिए यह पढ़ सकते हैं? (kyaa aap mere liye yeh paRh sakte hain?)
  4. जीते रहो, बेटा! तुमने मेरी बहुत मदद की। (jeete raho, beTaa! tumne meree bahut madad kee.)

Roleplay: lost and found. Round one — you're lost: your partner picks a real Delhi spot and gives directions at full Delhi speed. You must open with माफ़ कीजिए, क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?, interrupt at least once with मैं समझ नहीं पाया — धीरे बोल सकती हो? (she's tum: bol saktee ho), and repeat the directions back correctly. Round two — the tables turn: she asks YOU for help with five escalating tasks (carry this, read this, cook biryani, fix the wifi…); answer honestly with हाँ, मैं … कर सकता हूँ or नहीं, मैं … नहीं कर सकता. Real-world quest before the next lesson: ask one actual stranger for directions in Hindi — and report back.
chapters.book4-L18:
Lesson 18 Making Plans with Friends

The scene: Friday evening at the flat. Kabir has come over "for five minutes" (ninety minutes ago), the fans are on, the sky is doing its dramatic pre-monsoon act, and the eternal Delhi question is on the table: what's the Sunday plan? This is the subjunctive's home game — चलें? chalen? [chuh-lay(n)] "shall we?" — plus अगर…तो agar…to for all the backup plans a Delhi sky demands.

Dialogue: संडे का क्या प्लान है? sanDe kaa kyaa plaan hai?

Kabir:
और भाई! संडे का क्या प्लान है?
aur bhaaee! sanDe kaa kyaa plaan hai? [awr bhah-ee! sun-Day kah kyah plahn heh]
So, bhai! What's the plan for Sunday?
Jacob:
कोई प्लान नहीं। कहीं चलें?
koee plaan naheen. kaheen chalen? [koh-ee plahn nuh-hee(n). kuh-hee(n) chuh-lay(n)]
No plan. Shall we go somewhere?
Priya:
हाँ, चलें! मूवी देखें?
haan, chalen! moovee dekhen? [hah(n), chuh-lay(n)! moo-vee day-khay(n)]
Yes, let's! Shall we watch a movie?
Kabir:
नहीं यार, मूवी तो हमने पिछले संडे ही देखी थी।
naheen yaar, moovee to hamne pichhle sanDe hee dekhee thee. [nuh-hee(n) yahr, moo-vee toh hum-nay pich-lay sun-Day hee day-khee thee]
No yaar, we watched a movie just last Sunday.
Jacob:
तो बाहर खाना खाएँ? लेकिन कहाँ जाएँ?
to baahar khaanaa khaaen? lekin kahaan jaaen? [toh bah-hur khah-nah khah-ay(n)? lay-kin kuh-hah(n) jah-ay(n)]
Then shall we eat out? But where should we go?
Priya:
इंडिया गेट चलें? शाम को वहाँ अच्छा लगता है।
inDiyaa geT chalen? shaam ko vahaan achchhaa lagtaa hai. [in-Di-yah gayT chuh-lay(n)? shahm koh vuh-hah(n) uch-chhah lug-tah heh]
Shall we go to India Gate? It's nice there in the evening.
Kabir:
नहीं भाई, आजकल बहुत गरमी है। और मच्छर भी।
naheen bhaaee, aajkal bahut garmee hai. aur machchhar bhee. [nuh-hee(n) bhah-ee, ahj-kul buh-hut gur-mee heh. awr much-chhur bhee]
No bhai, it's really hot these days. And mosquitoes too.
Jacob:
और अगर बारिश हुई तो? आसमान देखो — काले बादल हैं।
aur agar baarish huee to? aasmaan dekho — kaale baadal hain. [awr uh-gur bah-rish hu-ee toh? ahs-mahn day-khoh — kah-lay bah-dul heh(n)]
And what if it rains? Look at the sky — black clouds.
Priya:
हाँ, शायद आज रात बारिश हो।
haan, shaayad aaj raat baarish ho. [hah(n), shah-yud ahj raht bah-rish hoh]
Yes, it might rain tonight. (shaayad + subjunctive = a real maybe)
Kabir:
तो सुनो — अगर बारिश हुई तो मेरे घर आओ। मम्मी पकौड़े बनाएँगी!
to suno — agar baarish huee to mere ghar aao. mummy pakauRe banaaengee! [toh su-noh — uh-gur bah-rish hu-ee toh may-ray ghur ah-oh. mum-mee puh-kaw-Ray buh-nah-ay(n)-gee]
Then listen — if it rains, come to my place. Mummy will make pakoras! (rain + pakoras: the sacred pairing)
Jacob:
और अगर बारिश नहीं हुई तो?
aur agar baarish naheen huee to? [awr uh-gur bah-rish nuh-hee(n) hu-ee toh]
And if it doesn't rain?
Kabir:
तो करोल बाग़ चलेंगे! वहाँ के छोले-भटूरे… क्या बताऊँ, भाई!
to karol baag chalenge! vahaan ke chhole-bhaTure… kyaa bataaoon, bhaaee! [toh kuh-rohl bahg chuh-lay(n)-gay! vuh-hah(n) kay chhoh-lay bhuh-Too-ray… kyah buh-tah-oo(n), bhah-ee]
Then we'll go to Karol Bagh! The chhole bhature there… what can I even say, bhai!
Priya:
मंज़ूर! लेकिन एक शर्त पर — हम मेट्रो से चलेंगे, तुम्हारी बाइक पर नहीं।
manzoor! lekin ek shart par — ham meTro se chalenge, tumhaaree baaik par naheen. [mun-zoor! lay-kin ayk shurt pur — hum may-Troh say chuh-lay(n)-gay, tum-hah-ree bah-ik pur nuh-hee(n)]
Agreed! But on one condition — we go by metro, not on your bike.
Kabir:
ठीक है। तो पक्का — संडे, बारह बजे, करोल बाग़ मेट्रो स्टेशन पर मिलें?
Theek hai. to pakkaa — sanDe, baarah baje, karol baag meTro sTeshan par milen? [Theek heh. toh puk-kah — sun-Day, bah-ruh buh-jay, kuh-rohl bahg may-Troh sTay-shun pur mi-lay(n)]
Okay. So it's fixed — Sunday, twelve o'clock, shall we meet at Karol Bagh metro station?
Priya:
पक्का! और कबीर — अगर तुम देर से आओ तो फ़ोन करना। तुम हमेशा देर से आते हो!
pakkaa! aur Kabir — agar tum der se aao to fon karnaa. tum hameshaa der se aate ho! [puk-kah! awr kuh-beer — uh-gur tum dayr say ah-oh toh fohn kur-nah. tum huh-may-shah dayr say ah-tay hoh]
Fixed! And Kabir — if you're running late, call. You're always late!
Kabir:
इस बार देर नहीं होगी। वादा!
is baar der naheen hogee. vaadaa! [is bahr dayr nuh-hee(n) hoh-gee. vah-dah]
This time there'll be no delay. Promise! (der (f) → hogee. Nobody believes him.)

Key phrases

कहीं चलें?kaheen chalen?kuh-hee(n) chuh-lay(n)shall we go somewhere?
कहाँ जाएँ?kahaan jaaen?kuh-hah(n) jah-ay(n)where should we go?
शायद बारिश होshaayad baarish hoshah-yud bah-rish hohit might rain
अगर बारिश हुई तो…agar baarish huee to…uh-gur bah-rish hu-ee tohif it (actually) rains, then…

मच्छरmachchhar (m)much-chhurmosquito (a Delhi stakeholder)

The plan-making machine

MovePatternExample
suggestsubjunctive + ?चलें? देखें? खाएँ? मिलें? chalen? dekhen? khaaen? milen?
ask the groupquestion word + subjunctiveकहाँ जाएँ? कितने बजे मिलें? kahaan jaaen? kitne baje milen?
real conditionअगर + future, तो + futureअगर टाइम होगा तो हम ज़रूर आएँगे। agar Taim hogaa to ham zaroor aaenge.
"if it happens"अगर + past form, तो + futureअगर बारिश हुई तो घर पर रहेंगे। agar baarish huee to ghar par rahenge.
"should it happen"अगर + subjunctive, तो + -ना commandअगर तुम देर से आओ तो फ़ोन करना। agar tum der se aao to fon karnaa.

Three cousins that all look like "go": चलें? chalen? is a suggestion — "shall we?"; चलो chalo is the nudge — "come on, let's move"; चलोगे? chaloge? is a future question — "will you come along?" (the same one you fired at the auto driver in Lesson 11). Pick by what you want back: an opinion, a body in motion, or a yes/no.

English lets you say "If it rains, we'll stay home" — no "then." Hindi will not: the तो to is structural, not optional. ✗ अगर बारिश हुई, हम घर पर रहेंगे sounds broken to every Hindi ear. Say अगर बारिश हुई तो हम घर पर रहेंगे। In fast speech Delhiites happily drop the agar — बारिश हुई तो नहीं जाएँगे baarish huee to naheen jaaenge — but the to survives every time. Drop the front, never the middle.

Delhi plan physics, memorize now: a plan is a rough draft until पक्का? has been asked and answered three separate times. देखते हैं dekhte hain [daykh-tay heh(n)] "we'll see" is a soft no. निकल रहा हूँ nikal rahaa hoon "I'm leaving now" means the shower is being considered. And the street way to open the whole negotiation is pure Delhi: सीन क्या है? seen kyaa hai? [seen kyah heh] — "what's the scene?" Use it on Kabir; watch him grin.

Chhole bhature is not "a dish" in Delhi; it's a Sunday-morning institution — spiced chickpeas with pillowy fried bread, born in the Punjabi refugee kitchens that remade the city after 1947. The famous shops (Karol Bagh, Paharganj, Kamla Nagar) sell out before noon, everyone eats standing up, and one plate is genuinely a two-person project. Pair with sweet lassi, then cancel all remaining plans: the post-bhature nap is also part of the tradition.

Comprehension

Exercise 18A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 18.

  1. कबीर किस दिन का प्लान बना रहा है? (Kabir kis din kaa plaan banaa rahaa hai?)
  2. उन्होंने मूवी कब देखी थी? (unhonne moovee kab dekhee thee?)
  3. अगर बारिश हुई तो वे लोग कहाँ जाएँगे? (agar baarish huee to voh log kahaan jaaenge?)
  4. कबीर की मम्मी क्या बनाएँगी? (Kabir kee mummy kyaa banaaengee?)
  5. प्रिया की शर्त क्या है? (Priya kee shart kyaa hai?)

Pattern drill: suggest it, condition it

Exercise 18B — Shall we? / If…then…

Items 1–4: turn the statement into a "shall we?" suggestion (subjunctive + ?). Items 5–8: join the two sentences with अगर…तो agar…to. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 18.

  1. हम चलते हैं। (ham chalte hain.)
  2. हम चाय पीते हैं। (ham chaay peete hain.)
  3. हम इंडिया गेट जाते हैं। (ham inDiyaa geT jaate hain.)
  4. हम कबीर से मिलते हैं। (ham Kabir se milte hain.)
  5. बारिश होगी। + हम घर पर रहेंगे। (baarish hogee. + ham ghar par rahenge.)
  6. मौसम अच्छा होगा। + हम बाहर खाएँगे। (mausam achchhaa hogaa. + ham baahar khaaenge.)
  7. तुम देर से आओगे। + मैं फ़ोन करूँगा। (tum der se aaoge. + main fon karoongaa.)
  8. टाइम होगा। + हम मूवी भी देखेंगे। (Taim hogaa. + ham moovee bhee dekhenge.)

Translation practice

Exercise 18C — Into Hindi

Write in Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 18.

  1. Shall we go somewhere on Sunday?
  2. Maybe it will rain tonight.
  3. If it rains, we will stay home.
  4. If you (tum) come late, call me. (gentle -naa command)

Exercise 18D — Into English

  1. कहाँ मिलें — घर पर या स्टेशन पर? (kahaan milen — ghar par yaa sTeshan par?)
  2. शायद वह देर से आए। (shaayad voh der se aae.)
  3. अगर टाइम होगा तो हम इंडिया गेट भी चलेंगे। (agar Taim hogaa to ham inDiyaa geT bhee chalenge.)
  4. चलो, पक्का हुआ — संडे को छोले-भटूरे! (chalo, pakkaa huaa — sanDe ko chhole-bhaTure!)

Roleplay: the great indecision. Plan your real next weekend, Delhi style. Rules: every proposal must be a subjunctive question (चलें? देखें? खाएँ?), and your partner must reject your first two ideas on principle (heat, mosquitoes, "we just did that") before accepting the third. Close the deal properly: पक्का? — पक्का! — plus a time (कितने बजे मिलें?). Then play backup plans: take turns building अगर…तो chains, each sillier than the last — अगर ऑटो नहीं मिला तो हम घोड़े पर चलेंगे "if we don't find an auto, we'll go by horse." Last one to break into English wins.
chapters.book4-L19:
Lesson 19 Sabzi Mandi

The scene: Sunday morning, the vegetable market near the flat — crates of tomatoes glowing in the sun, weighing scales clanging, forty vendors shouting forty prices. Jacob has announced that today HE will do the bargaining. Priya has come along purely for the entertainment. Today's weapons: क्या भाव है? kyaa bhaav hai? [kyah bhahv heh] and the holy trinity of quantities — kilo, aadhaa kilo, paav.

Dialogue: आज मोल-भाव मैं करूँगा aaj mol-bhaav main karoongaa

Priya:
थैला लिया? आज मंडी में बहुत भीड़ होगी।
thailaa liyaa? aaj manDee mein bahut bheeR hogee. [theh-lah li-yah? ahj mun-Dee may(n) buh-hut bheeR hoh-gee]
Got the bag? The mandi will be really crowded today. (bheeR (f) crowd)
Jacob:
हाँ जी! और आज मोल-भाव मैं करूँगा। तुम बस देखो।
haan jee! aur aaj mol-bhaav main karoongaa. tum bas dekho. [hah(n) jee! awr ahj mohl-bhahv meh(n) kuh-roo(n)-gah. tum bus day-khoh]
Yes ma'am! And today I'm doing the bargaining. You just watch.
Priya:
अच्छा? चलो, देखते हैं!
achchhaa? chalo, dekhte hain! [uch-chhah? chuh-loh, daykh-tay heh(n)]
Oh really? Well then — let's see!
Jacob:
भैया, टमाटर क्या भाव है?
bhaiyaa, TamaaTar kyaa bhaav hai? [bheh-yah, Tuh-mah-Tur kyah bhahv heh]
Bhaiya, what's the rate for tomatoes?
Sabzi-vaalaa:
साठ रुपये किलो, साहब। एकदम ताज़े हैं।
saaTh rupaye kilo, saahab. ekdam taaze hain. [sahTh ru-puh-yay ki-loh, sah-hub. ayk-dum tah-zay heh(n)]
Sixty rupees a kilo, sir. Absolutely fresh.
Jacob:
साठ?! भैया, पिछले हफ़्ते तो चालीस रुपये किलो थे!
saaTh?! bhaiyaa, pichhle hafte to chaalees rupaye kilo the! [sahTh?! bheh-yah, pich-lay huf-tay toh chah-lees ru-puh-yay ki-loh thay]
Sixty?! Bhaiya, last week they were forty a kilo!
Sabzi-vaalaa:
क्या करें साहब, बारिश की वजह से सब महँगा है।
kyaa karen saahab, baarish kee vajah se sab mehngaa hai. [kyah kuh-ray(n) sah-hub, bah-rish kee vuh-juh say sub meh(n)-gah heh]
What can one do, sir — because of the rain everything's expensive. (kyaa karen — the great subjunctive shrug)
Jacob:
अच्छा, ऐसा करो — दो किलो दो, पचास रुपये किलो।
achchhaa, aisaa karo — do kilo do, pachaas rupaye kilo. [uch-chhah, eh-sah kuh-roh — doh ki-loh doh, puh-chahs ru-puh-yay ki-loh]
Okay, do this — give me two kilos, at fifty a kilo. (aisaa karo = "let's do this" — the deal-maker's opener)
Sabzi-vaalaa:
पचपन, साहब। आख़िरी भाव।
pachpan, saahab. aakhiree bhaav. [puch-pun, sah-hub. ah-khi-ree bhahv]
Fifty-five, sir. Final rate.
Jacob:
ठीक है, पचपन। और आधा किलो भिंडी, एक पाव हरी मिर्च।
Theek hai, pachpan. aur aadhaa kilo bhinDee, ek paav haree mirch. [Theek heh, puch-pun. awr ah-dhah ki-loh bhin-Dee, ayk pahv huh-ree mirch]
Fine, fifty-five. And half a kilo of okra, one paav of green chilies. (paav = quarter kilo, 250 g)
Sabzi-vaalaa:
और कुछ, साहब? आलू, प्याज़? एकदम सस्ते हैं।
aur kuchh, saahab? aaloo, pyaaz? ekdam saste hain. [awr kuchh, sah-hub? ah-loo, pyahz? ayk-dum suhs-tay heh(n)]
Anything else, sir? Potatoes, onions? Dirt cheap.
Jacob:
हाँ, एक किलो प्याज़। बस। …और भैया — धनिया?
haan, ek kilo pyaaz. bas. …aur bhaiyaa — dhaniyaa? [hah(n), ayk ki-loh pyahz. bus. awr bheh-yah — dhuh-ni-yah]
Yes, one kilo of onions. That's it. …And bhaiya — coriander? (the sacred question — see the culture box)
Sabzi-vaalaa:
धनिया-मिर्ची फ़्री में, साहब! आप पुराने ग्राहक हैं।
dhaniyaa-mirchee free mein, saahab! aap puraane graahak hain. [dhuh-ni-yah mir-chee free may(n), sah-hub! ahp pu-rah-nay grah-huk heh(n)]
Coriander and chilies free, sir! You're an old customer.
Priya:
वाह! अब तुम सच में दिल्ली वाले हो!
vaah! ab tum sach mein dillee vaale ho! [vah! ub tum such may(n) dil-lee vah-lay hoh]
Wow! Now you really are a Delhi-wala!
Jacob:
और देखो — पैसे भी बचे!
aur dekho — paise bhee bache! [awr day-khoh — peh-say bhee buh-chay]
And look — money left over too! (bachnaa (vi) = to be saved / left over)
Sabzi-vaalaa:
अगले हफ़्ते फिर आइए, साहब। आपके लिए स्पेशल भाव!
agle hafte phir aaiye, saahab. aapke liye speshal bhaav! [ug-lay huf-tay fir ah-i-yay, sah-hub. ahp-kay li-yay spay-shul bhahv]
Come again next week, sir. Special rate for you! (he says this to everyone)

250 gएक पावek paavayk pahv
500 gआधा किलोaadhaa kiloah-dhah ki-loh
750 gतीन पावteen paavteen pahv
1 kgएक किलोek kiloayk ki-loh
1½ kgडेढ़ किलोDeRh kiloDayRh ki-loh
2½ kgढाई किलोDhaaee kiloDhah-ee ki-loh
a dozen (bananas!)एक दर्जनek darjan (m)ayk dur-jun

Quantity grammar is mercifully simple: amount + thing, no "of," no postposition — आधा किलो प्याज़ aadhaa kilo pyaaz, दो किलो टमाटर do kilo TamaaTar. Prices work the same way: पचास रुपये किलो pachaas rupaye kilo "fifty rupees a/per kilo." And keep your two price-questions straight: क्या भाव है? for produce by weight, कितने का है? kitne kaa hai? [kit-nay kah heh] for a thing with one price.

Watch the plural agreement hiding in the vegetables. TamaaTar, aaloo, pyaaz in the market are masculine plurals: टमाटर ताज़े हैं TamaaTar taaze hain — not ✗ ताज़ा है. But bhinDee and mirch run feminine: भिंडी ताज़ी है bhinDee taazee hai. When you order, the verb is a friendly tum-imperative or the casual -naa: आधा किलो भिंडी देना — Lesson 11's machinery, now buying dinner.

The sacred free dhaniyaa. In every Indian sabzi mandi there is an unwritten contract: buy your vegetables, then ask — भैया, धनिया-मिर्ची? bhaiyaa, dhaniyaa-mirchee? [bheh-yah, dhuh-ni-yah mir-chee] — and a fistful of fresh coriander and green chilies lands in your bag, फ़्री में. This is not begging; it is protocol, as fixed as the moon. Paying for coriander marks you as a tourist; forgetting to ask marks you as hopeless. A vendor who refuses (rare, scandalous) forfeits the relationship forever. Priya's family has bought from the same sabzi-vaalaa for twenty years — that, too, is the dhaniyaa economy at work.

Mandi soundtrack: vendors sing their prices — ले लो ले लो, बीस का दो किलो! le lo le lo, bees kaa do kilo! [lay loh lay loh, bees kah doh ki-loh] "take it, take it, two kilos for twenty!" (That doubled le lo is a compound verb — Unit 19's machinery, starring in the very next lesson. For now, just enjoy the song.) Every colony has a weekly evening bazaar — सोम बाज़ार, बुध बाज़ार som baazaar, budh baazaar (Monday market, Wednesday market) — where rates drop as the night gets later. Bring your own thailaa; and yes, the walk-away trick from Lesson 11 (रहने दो, भैया) works on vegetables too. It works on everything.

Comprehension

Exercise 19A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 19.

  1. आज टमाटर क्या भाव है? (aaj TamaaTar kyaa bhaav hai?)
  2. सब कुछ महँगा क्यों है? (sab kuchh mehngaa kyon hai?)
  3. जैकब कितने किलो टमाटर लेता है? (Jacob kitne kilo TamaaTar letaa hai?)
  4. धनिया-मिर्ची कितने की है? (dhaniyaa-mirchee kitne kee hai?)

Pattern drill: the shopping list

  2. half a kilo of tomatoes

  2. Give me half a kilo of tomatoes and one paav of green chilies.

Exercise 19D — Into English

  1. बारिश की वजह से आज सब्ज़ी महँगी है। (baarish kee vajah se aaj sabzee mehngee hai.)
  2. एकदम ताज़े हैं साहब — अभी मंडी से आए हैं। (ekdam taaze hain saahab — abhee manDee se aae hain.)
  3. अच्छा, आख़िरी भाव पचास — लेना है तो लो। (achchhaa, aakhiree bhaav pachaas — lenaa hai to lo.)
  4. अगले हफ़्ते फिर आइए — आपके लिए स्पेशल भाव! (agle hafte phir aaiye — aapke liye speshal bhaav!)

Roleplay: mandi wars. Raid the kitchen for real vegetables and set up shop. Your partner is the vendor and quotes everything at double. Your mission, all in Hindi: (1) ask the rate of three vegetables with क्या भाव है?, (2) order in three different quantities — a kilo, an aadhaa kilo, and a paav, (3) knock at least one price down with थोड़ा कम करो and a counter-number, (4) close by claiming your free धनिया-मिर्ची. Then swap roles — as the vendor, you must sing at least one ले लो ले लो sales cry. Real-world quest: do the actual vegetable run solo this week. Score double if you come home with free dhaniyaa.
chapters.book4-L20:
Lesson 20 Telling a Story

The scene: A muggy evening, and — right on cue — the power cuts out. No wifi, no TV, one candle. Which is exactly how the best Hindi happens: Priya tells a story from her Delhi childhood, and it arrives absolutely loaded with Unit 19's compound verbs — ho gayaa, kho gaee, mil gaee, aa gae, le diyaa, de diyaa. Then it's Jacob's turn to tell his day the same way. Listen for the flavors: le = for yourself, de = for someone else, jaa = tipped into a new state.

Dialogue: फिर क्या हुआ? phir kyaa huaa?

Jacob:
अरे! बिजली चली गई!
arre! bijlee chalee gaee! [uh-ray! bij-lee chuh-lee guh-ee]
Hey! The power's gone! (bijlee (f) electricity; chalaa jaanaa = to go away)
Priya:
फिर से?! कोई बात नहीं। मोमबत्ती जला दो — मेज़ पर है।
phir se?! koee baat naheen. mombattee jalaa do — mez par hai. [fir say?! koh-ee baht nuh-hee(n). mohm-but-tee juh-lah doh — mayz pur heh]
Again?! Never mind. Light the candle — it's on the table. (mombattee (f) candle; jalaa do — do it for us both)
Jacob:
हो गया। अब?
ho gayaa. ab? [hoh guh-yah. ub]
Done. Now what?
Priya:
अब बैठ जाओ। मैं तुम्हें अपने बचपन की एक बात बताती हूँ।
ab baiTh jaao. main tumhen apne bachpan kee ek baat bataatee hoon. [ub behTh jah-oh. meh(n) tum-hay(n) up-nay buch-pun kee ayk baht buh-tah-tee hoo(n)]
Now sit down. Let me tell you something from my childhood. (bachpan (m) childhood)
Jacob:
हाँ-हाँ, बताओ!
haan-haan, bataao! [hah(n)-hah(n), buh-tah-oh]
Yes, yes — tell me!
Priya:
मैं आठ साल की थी, दिवाली का मेला था।
पापा ने मुझे एक लाल गुब्बारा ले दिया — मैं बहुत ख़ुश हो गई।
main aaTh saal kee thee, divaalee kaa melaa thaa. paapaa ne mujhe ek laal gubbaaraa le diyaa — main bahut khush ho gaee. [meh(n) ahTh sahl kee thee, di-vah-lee kah may-lah thah. pah-pah nay mu-jhay ayk lahl gub-bah-rah lay di-yah — meh(n) buh-hut khush hoh guh-ee]
I was eight; it was the Diwali fair. Papa bought me a red balloon — I was overjoyed. (melaa (m) fair; gubbaaraa (m) balloon; le diyaa = got-and-gave, bought for me)
Jacob:
अच्छा, फिर?
achchhaa, phir? [uch-chhah, fir]
Okay — then?
Priya:
फिर अचानक बहुत भीड़ आ गई, पापा का हाथ छूट गया… और मैं खो गई।
phir achaanak bahut bheeR aa gaee, paapaa kaa haath chhooT gayaa… aur main kho gaee. [fir uh-chah-nuk buh-hut bheeR ah guh-ee, pah-pah kah hahth chhooT guh-yah… awr meh(n) khoh guh-ee]
Then suddenly a big crowd came, Papa's hand slipped away… and I got lost. (chhooTnaa (vi) = to slip loose; kho jaanaa = to get lost)
Jacob:
अरे नहीं! फिर क्या हुआ?
arre naheen! phir kyaa huaa? [uh-ray nuh-hee(n)! fir kyah hu-ah]
Oh no! Then what happened? (the listener's sacred duty — keep asking this)
Priya:
मैं रो पड़ी। एक चाय वाले ने मुझे देखा।
उसने मुझे पानी दे दिया और बोला — "बेटा, यहीं बैठो।"
main ro paRee. ek chaay vaale ne mujhe dekhaa. usne mujhe paanee de diyaa aur bolaa — "beTaa, yaheen baiTho." [meh(n) roh puh-Ree. ayk chah-ay vah-lay nay mu-jhay day-khah. us-nay mu-jhay pah-nee day di-yah awr boh-lah — bay-Tah, yuh-hee(n) beh-Thoh]
I burst into tears. A chai-vaalaa saw me. He gave me water and said, "Beta, sit right here." (ro paRee — the sudden-burst vector from Unit 19)
Jacob:
और पापा?
aur paapaa? [awr pah-pah]
And Papa?
Priya:
दस मिनट के बाद पापा आ गए — बहुत परेशान थे!
उन्होंने मुझे गोद में उठा लिया।
और मुझे एक बड़ी कुल्फ़ी भी मिल गई!
das minaT ke baad paapaa aa gae — bahut pareshaan the! unhonne mujhe god mein uThaa liyaa. aur mujhe ek baRee kulfee bhee mil gaee! [dus mi-nuT kay bahd pah-pah ah guh-ay — buh-hut puh-ray-shahn thay! un-hoh(n)-nay mu-jhay gohd may(n) u-Thah li-yah. awr mu-jhay ayk buh-Ree kul-fee bhee mil guh-ee]
Ten minutes later Papa arrived — so worried! He scooped me up in his arms. And I even scored a big kulfi! (god (f) lap; uThaa liyaa = swept up (to himself); mil gaee — kulfee (f))
Jacob:
और गुब्बारा?
aur gubbaaraa? [awr gub-bah-rah]
And the balloon?
Priya:
गुब्बारा तो उड़ गया था! लेकिन कुल्फ़ी के बाद मैं उसे भूल गई।
…अब तुम बताओ — आज तुम्हारा दिन कैसा था?
असली दिल्ली स्टाइल में!
gubbaaraa to uR gayaa thaa! lekin kulfee ke baad main use bhool gaee. …ab tum bataao — aaj tumhaaraa din kaisaa thaa? asalee dillee sTaail mein! [gub-bah-rah toh uR guh-yah thah! lay-kin kul-fee kay bahd meh(n) u-say bhool guh-ee. ub tum buh-tah-oh — ahj tum-hah-rah din keh-sah thah? uh-suh-lee dil-lee sTah-il may(n)]
The balloon had flown off! But after the kulfi I forgot all about it. …Now you tell me — how was your day? Real Delhi style! (uR jaanaa = to fly away; bhool jaanaa = to forget)
Jacob:
सुनो। आज सुबह मेरा मेट्रो कार्ड खो गया। मैंने नया ले लिया।
ऑफ़िस का काम ख़त्म हो गया, बॉस को रिपोर्ट दे दी,
और शाम को मैं घर आ गया। बस!
…अब मुझे भी कुल्फ़ी मिल सकती है?
suno. aaj subah meraa meTro kaarD kho gayaa. maine nayaa le liyaa. ofis kaa kaam khatam ho gayaa, baus ko riporT de dee, aur shaam ko main ghar aa gayaa. bas! …ab mujhe bhee kulfee mil saktee hai? [su-noh. ahj su-beh may-rah may-Troh kahrD khoh guh-yah. meh(n)-nay nuh-yah lay li-yah. aw-fis kah kahm khuh-tum hoh guh-yah, baws koh ri-porT day dee, awr shahm koh meh(n) ghur ah guh-yah. bus! ub mu-jhay bhee kul-fee mil suk-tee heh]
Listen. This morning my metro card got lost. I got myself a new one. The office work got finished, I handed the boss the report, and in the evening I came home. That's it! …So can I have a kulfi now too? (riporT (f) → de dee)
Priya:
परफ़ेक्ट! तुमने तो हिन्दी सीख ली!
parfekT! tumne to hindee seekh lee! [pur-fekT! tum-nay toh hin-dee seekh lee]
Perfect! You've really gone and learned Hindi! (seekh lee — got it under your belt; hindee (f) → lee)

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
बिजली चली गईbijlee chalee gaeebij-lee chuh-lee guh-eethe power went out

मिल गया / मिल गईmil gayaa / mil gaeemil guh-yah / guh-eeturned up, was gotten

Vector flavors, story edition

VectorFlavorIn Priya's storyने?
लेना lenaatoward yourselfउठा लिया, ले लिया uThaa liyaa, le liyaayes
देना denaatoward someone elseले दिया, दे दिया, दे दी le diyaa, de diyaa, de deeyes
जाना jaanaatipped into a new stateखो गई, आ गए, उड़ गया, भूल गई kho gaee, aa gae, uR gayaa, bhool gaeenever
पड़ना paRnaasudden burstरो पड़ी ro paReenever

The ne rule is sacred: ने follows the vector, not the main verb. Same story, both directions: मैंने नया कार्ड ले लिया maine nayaa kaarD le liyaa — lenaa is transitive, so ne appears and liyaa agrees with the card. But मेरा कार्ड खो गया meraa kaarD kho gayaa and मैं घर आ गया main ghar aa gayaa — jaanaa is intransitive, so ne is banned. ✗ मैंने खो गया, ✗ मैंने आ गया — never. And watch the feminine ripple: रिपोर्ट दे दी riporT de dee, because riporT is (f).

Notice what holds a Hindi story together — not fancy connectors, just फिर phir "then," अचानक achaanak "suddenly," …के बाद ke baad "after…," and a listener doing their job. Storytelling in India is a team sport: the audience must supply अच्छा?, अरे नहीं!, फिर क्या हुआ? at regular intervals, or the teller will stop and check whether you have died.

Delhi never says "power outage" — it says लाइट चली गई! laaiT chalee gaee! [lah-iT chuh-lee guh-ee], and when it returns, the whole block cheers आ गई! aa gaee! like India won the toss. The soundtrack in between: the inverter's beep, neighbors drifting to balconies, and someone's confident forecast — अभी आ जाएगी। abhee aa jaaegee. [uh-bhee ah jah-ay-gee] "It'll be back any minute." This is Unit 19's promise-tense (ho jaaegaa) applied to the electrical grid, with the same reliability.

Every Indian family owns a lost-at-the-mela story — a child, a crowd, a balloon, a rescue, and a sweet at the end. Diwali fairs, Dussehra grounds, wedding crowds: the settings vary, the plot never does. When Priya's parents hear Jacob ask फिर क्या हुआ? in the right places, he isn't just practicing grammar — he's performing the oldest role in the family living room: the good listener.

Comprehension

Exercise 20A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 20.

  1. कहानी में प्रिया कितने साल की थी? (kahaanee mein Priya kitne saal kee thee?)
  2. पापा ने प्रिया को क्या ले दिया? (paapaa ne Priya ko kyaa le diyaa?)
  3. प्रिया कहाँ खो गई? (Priya kahaan kho gaee?)
  4. चाय वाले ने प्रिया को क्या दे दिया? (chaay vaale ne Priya ko kyaa de diyaa?)
  5. जैकब का क्या खो गया? (Jacob kaa kyaa kho gayaa?)

Pattern drill: add the flavor

Exercise 20B — Bare verb → compound verb

Rewrite with the vector in brackets. Watch ने and agreement — the vector decides both. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 20.

  1. मैंने चाय पी। (maine chaay pee.) → [+ lenaa]
  2. मैंने पैसे दिए। (maine paise diye.) → [+ denaa]

  5. दूध ख़त्म हुआ। (doodh khatam huaa.) → [+ jaanaa]
  6. मैंने नया फ़ोन लिया। (maine nayaa fon liyaa.) → [+ lenaa]
  7. उसने मुझे सब बताया। (usne mujhe sab bataayaa.) → [+ denaa]

Translation practice

Exercise 20C — Into Hindi

Use a compound verb in every answer. Write Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 20.

  1. The power went out.
  2. My metro card got lost.
  3. I got (myself) a new card.
  4. Don't worry — it'll get done.

Exercise 20D — Into English

  1. पापा आ गए और हम घर चले गए। (paapaa aa gae aur ham ghar chale gae.)
  2. उसने मुझे अपना नंबर दे दिया। (usne mujhe apnaa nambar de diyaa.)
  3. अरे! मैं अपना थैला मंडी में भूल गया! (arre! main apnaa thailaa manDee mein bhool gayaa!)
  4. टेंशन मत लो यार — सब ठीक हो जाएगा। (Tenshan mat lo yaar — sab Theek ho jaaegaa.)

Roleplay: story night. Lights low, candle optional. Round one: your partner tells a true childhood story, slowly; your job is to count the compound verbs on your fingers and to interrupt with फिर क्या हुआ? and अरे नहीं! at least twice each — in the right places. Round two: retell today's real day with a minimum of five compounds (kho gayaa, le liyaa, de diyaa, ho gayaa, aa gayaa…); she referees the ने rule — one pretend rupee fine per wrong ne. Round three, the hard one: retell HER childhood story back to her in your own Hindi. Kulfi for the finisher.

Items 23–25: circle or write the right vector form. Item 26: circle the correct sentence — remember, ने follows the vector.

  1. मेरा कार्ड खो ___। [gayaa / liyaa / diyaa]

chapters.book4-L21:
Lesson 21 Describing People

The scene: Neha di's wedding-anniversary party — two rooms of relatives, half of whom Jacob has met exactly once. Tonight's survival tool is Unit 21's paired relative: जो…वह jo…voh — "the one who… that one." Point with a whole clause: जो आदमी वहाँ खड़ा है… jo aadmee vahaan khaRaa hai… [joh ahd-mee vuh-hah(n) khuh-Rah heh]. Also on the guest list: Sharma aunty, the colony's legendary matchmaker. Jacob has been warned.

Dialogue: वह कौन है जो…? voh kaun hai jo…?

Priya:
तैयार हो? अंदर बहुत लोग हैं — और सब तुमसे मिलना चाहते हैं।
taiyaar ho? andar bahut log hain — aur sab tumse milnaa chaahte hain. [teh-yahr hoh? un-dur buh-hut lohg heh(n) — awr sub tum-say mil-nah chah-tay heh(n)]
Ready? There are a lot of people inside — and they all want to meet you.
Jacob:
मदद करो — मुझे आधे नाम भी याद नहीं हैं!
madad karo — mujhe aadhe naam bhee yaad naheen hain! [muh-dud kuh-roh — mu-jhay ah-dhay nahm bhee yahd nuh-hee(n) heh(n)]
Help me — I don't even remember half the names!
Priya:
आसान है। जो अंकल सोफ़े पर बैठे हैं, वे नेहा दी के ससुर हैं।
aasaan hai. jo ankal sofe par baiThe hain, voh Neha dee ke sasur hain. [ah-sahn heh. joh un-kul soh-fay pur beh-Thay heh(n), voh nay-hah dee kay suh-sur heh(n)]
Easy. The uncle sitting on the sofa is Neha di's father-in-law. (respect plurals all through the jo-clause: baiThe hain… hain)
Jacob:
और वह आदमी कौन है जो खिड़की के पास खड़ा है? लंबा, चश्मे वाला।
aur voh aadmee kaun hai jo khiRkee ke paas khaRaa hai? lambaa, chashme vaalaa. [awr voh ahd-mee kawn heh joh khiR-kee kay pahs khuh-Rah heh? lum-bah, chush-may vah-lah]
And who's the man standing by the window? Tall, with glasses. (flipped order — the voh-half first, jo-half second; both are fine)
Priya:
वह कबीर का बड़ा भाई है — डॉक्टर। थोड़ा शर्मीला है, कम बोलता है।
voh Kabir kaa baRaa bhaaee hai — DaukTar. thoRaa sharmeelaa hai, kam boltaa hai. [voh kuh-beer kah buh-Rah bhah-ee heh — Dauk-Tur. thoh-Rah shur-mee-lah heh, kum bohl-tah heh]
That's Kabir's older brother — a doctor. A bit shy; doesn't talk much.
Sharma aunty:
अरे! तुम प्रिया के पति हो न? जो अमेरिका से आए हो?
arre! tum Priya ke pati ho na? jo amreekaa se aae ho? [uh-ray! tum pri-yah kay puh-ti hoh nah? joh um-ree-kah say ah-ay hoh]
Oh! You're Priya's husband, right? The one who's come from America? (na? = "right?" — the friendly tag)
Jacob:
जी आंटी जी, मैं जैकब हूँ। नमस्ते!
jee aunty jee, main Jacob hoon. namaste! [jee ahn-Tee jee, meh(n) jay-kub hoo(n). nuh-muhs-tay]
Yes aunty-ji, I'm Jacob. Namaste!
Sharma aunty:
सुनो बेटा — वह लंबा लड़का कौन है जो वहाँ खड़ा है?
suno beTaa — voh lambaa laRkaa kaun hai jo vahaan khaRaa hai? [su-noh bay-Tah — voh lum-bah luhR-kah kawn heh joh vuh-hah(n) khuh-Rah heh]
Listen, beta — who's that tall boy standing over there?
Jacob:
जो आदमी वहाँ खड़ा है? वह प्रिया का भाई है — रोहन।
jo aadmee vahaan khaRaa hai? voh Priya kaa bhaaee hai — Rohan. [joh ahd-mee vuh-hah(n) khuh-Rah heh? voh pri-yah kah bhah-ee heh — roh-hun]
The man standing there? That's Priya's brother — Rohan.
Sharma aunty:
कितना अच्छा लड़का है! बेटा, उसके लिए मेरे पास एक बहुत अच्छी लड़की है — डॉक्टर है!
kitnaa achchhaa laRkaa hai! beTaa, uske liye mere paas ek bahut achchhee laRkee hai — DaukTar hai! [kit-nah uch-chhah luhR-kah heh! bay-Tah, us-kay li-yay may-ray pahs ayk buh-hut uch-chhee luhR-kee heh — Dauk-Tur heh]
What a nice boy! Beta, I have a very nice girl for him — she's a doctor! (the matchmaking engine starts in under a minute)
Jacob (laughing):
लेकिन आंटी जी, रोहन अभी बाईस साल का है!
lekin aunty jee, Rohan abhee baaees saal kaa hai! [lay-kin ahn-Tee jee, roh-hun uh-bhee bah-ees sahl kah heh]
But aunty-ji, Rohan is only twenty-two!
Sharma aunty:
तो क्या हुआ? जो लड़का आज छोटा है, वह कल बड़ा हो जाएगा!
to kyaa huaa? jo laRkaa aaj chhoTaa hai, voh kal baRaa ho jaaegaa! [toh kyah hu-ah? joh luhR-kah ahj chhoh-Tah heh, voh kul buh-Rah hoh jah-ay-gah]
So what? The boy who's young today will be grown tomorrow! (aunty logic, in perfect jo…voh form)
Priya:
आंटी जी, खाना लग गया है — आपके लिए प्लेट लाऊँ?
aunty jee, khaanaa lag gayaa hai — aapke liye pleT laaoon? [ahn-Tee jee, khah-nah lug guh-yah heh — ahp-kay li-yay playT lah-oo(n)]
Aunty-ji, dinner is served — shall I bring you a plate? (khaanaa lag gayaa = the food's been laid out; the world's politest rescue)
Sharma aunty:
हाँ बेटा, चलो। और जैकब — जो बात मैंने कही, वह याद रखना!
haan beTaa, chalo. aur Jacob — jo baat maine kahee, voh yaad rakhnaa! [hah(n) bay-Tah, chuh-loh. awr jay-kub — joh baht meh(n)-nay kuh-hee, voh yahd rukh-nah]
Yes beta, let's go. And Jacob — remember what I said! (jo baat… voh: even her exit line is a relative clause; baat (f) → kahee)
Jacob (to Priya):
अब समझ गया — दिल्ली की पार्टी में सब कुछ मिलता है: खाना, गाना… और रिश्ते!
ab samajh gayaa — dillee kee paarTee mein sab kuchh miltaa hai: khaanaa, gaanaa… aur rishte! [ub suh-mujh guh-yah — dil-lee kee pahr-Tee may(n) sub kuchh mil-tah heh: khah-nah, gah-nah… awr rish-tay]
Now I get it — at a Delhi party you can find everything: food, music… and marriage proposals! (rishtaa (m) = relation; also "a match/proposal")

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning

लंबा / लंबीlambaa / lambeelum-bah / lum-beetall
शर्मीलाsharmeelaashur-mee-lahshy
बातूनीbaatooneebah-too-neetalkative, a chatterbox

मज़ाकियाmazaakiyaamuh-zah-ki-yahfunny (Delhi also says fanee)

दाढ़ीdaaRhee (f)dah-Rheebeard
पति / पत्नीpati / patneepuh-ti / put-neehusband / wife
रिश्ताrishtaa (m)rish-tahrelation; a (marriage) match

The ask–relate–answer triangle

Question (k-)Relative (j-)Answer (v-/u-)Example
कौन kaunजो joवह vohजो गा रही है, वह मेरी बहन है।
किस kisजिस jisउस usजिस आदमी से तुम मिले, वह डॉक्टर है।
किसका kiskaaजिसका jiskaaउसका uskaaजिसकी दाढ़ी है, वह रोहन का दोस्त है।
कहाँ kahaanजहाँ jahaanवहाँ vahaanजहाँ खाना है, वहाँ सब लोग हैं।

Two traps at one party. First, the Unit 21 classic: the relative "who" is jo, never kaun — ✗ वह आदमी, कौन वहाँ खड़ा है is broken; kaun only asks. Second, respect travels into the clause: elders keep their plurals on both sides — जो अंकल बैठे हैं, वे नेहा के ससुर हैं. Saying baiThaa hai about somebody's father-in-law is a scandal with grammar attached.

Word order has two settings. Textbook setting: lead with the jo-half — जो आदमी वहाँ खड़ा है, वह रोहन है। Party setting: ask the voh-half first and hang the jo-clause after — वह आदमी कौन है जो वहाँ खड़ा है? Both are correct; the flipped one is how questions come out in real time. For quick descriptions without a full clause, Delhi grabs vaalaa instead: चश्मे वाला "the glasses guy" — full toolkit in Unit 24.

Field guide to the Delhi party: every man over forty is uncle, every woman aunty, no exceptions, no actual kinship required. And every party has a Sharma aunty — the volunteer matchmaking department. Her opening scan: बेटा, शादी हो गई? beTaa, shaadee ho gaee? [bay-Tah, shah-dee hoh guh-ee] "Married yet?" Jacob's cheat code, delivered with a big smile: जी, हो गई! jee, ho gaee! She means only love — being scanned is a form of adoption.

People-describing runs warmer and blunter in India than Americans expect: आप कितने स्मार्ट लग रहे हैं! "how smart (well-dressed) you're looking!" is normal party talk, and relatives will happily comment on your appearance in both directions. It's familiarity, not rudeness. Keep your own descriptions on the safe rails — lambaa, hoshiyaar, mazaakiyaa, sharmeelaa — and leave commentary on anyone's weight to their own mother, who will handle it thoroughly.

Comprehension

Exercise 21A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences — lead with जो where you can. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 21.

  1. जो अंकल सोफ़े पर बैठे हैं, वे कौन हैं? (jo ankal sofe par baiThe hain, voh kaun hain?)
  2. कबीर का बड़ा भाई क्या काम करता है? (Kabir kaa baRaa bhaaee kyaa kaam kartaa hai?)
  3. कबीर का भाई कैसा है? (Kabir kaa bhaaee kaisaa hai?)
  4. जो आदमी वहाँ खड़ा है, वह कौन है? (jo aadmee vahaan khaRaa hai, voh kaun hai?)
  5. आंटी जी के पास रोहन के लिए क्या है? (aunty jee ke paas Rohan ke liye kyaa hai?)

Pattern drill: two sentences into one

Exercise 21B — Build the jo…voh pair

Join with जो…वह (items 6–8 need jis/jin…us/un). Model: वह आदमी रोहन है + वह वहाँ खड़ा है → जो आदमी वहाँ खड़ा है, वह रोहन है। Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 21.

  1. वह आदमी रोहन है + वह वहाँ खड़ा है (voh aadmee Rohan hai + voh vahaan khaRaa hai)
  2. वह लड़की डॉक्टर है + वह पीली कमीज़ में है (voh laRkee DaukTar hai + voh peelee kameez mein hai)
  3. वे अंकल नेहा के ससुर हैं + वे सोफ़े पर बैठे हैं (voh ankal Neha ke sasur hain + voh sofe par baiThe hain)
  4. वह चाय बहुत अच्छी थी + तुमने वह चाय बनाई (voh chaay bahut achchhee thee + tumne voh chaay banaaee)
  5. वह लड़का कबीर का भाई है + वह चश्मा पहनता है (voh laRkaa Kabir kaa bhaaee hai + voh chashmaa pehntaa hai)
  6. वह आदमी हमारा पड़ोसी है + तुम उस आदमी से मिले (voh aadmee hamaaraa paRosee hai + tum us aadmee se mile)
  7. वह दुकान आज बंद है + हम उस दुकान से सब्ज़ी लेते हैं (voh dukaan aaj band hai + ham us dukaan se sabzee lete hain)
  8. वे लोग नहीं आए + मैंने उन लोगों को बुलाया (voh log naheen aae + maine un logon ko bulaayaa)

Translation practice

Exercise 21C — Into Hindi

Lead with the jo-half. Write Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 21.

  1. The man who is standing near the window is Kabir's older brother.
  2. The girl who is singing is very talkative.
  3. The uncle who is sitting on the sofa is Neha di's father-in-law. (respect plurals!)
  4. Whoever comes will get food. (jo bhee)

Exercise 21D — Into English

  1. जो आंटी हर पार्टी में रिश्तों की बात करती हैं, वे शर्मा आंटी हैं। (jo aunty har paarTee mein rishton kee baat kartee hain, voh Sharmaa aunty hain.)
  2. जिस लड़की से तुम मिले, वह नेहा की ननद है। (jis laRkee se tum mile, voh Neha kee nanad hai.) (nanad = husband's sister)
  3. जो लोग देर से आए, उन्हें ठंडा खाना मिला। (jo log der se aae, unhen ThanDaa khaanaa milaa.)
  4. जो होगा, देखा जाएगा! (jo hogaa, dekhaa jaaegaa!)

Roleplay: the party briefing. Open a phone gallery or a family-event album. Round one: point and ask each other वह कौन है जो…? — answers must lead with जो: जो आदमी दाढ़ी वाला है, वह मेरा चाचा है। Round two: your partner becomes Sharma aunty at full power — she interrogates you about three "guests" and you answer every question with a jo…voh sentence while dodging one matchmaking attempt politely. Round three: describe five real family members with two personality words each (hoshiyaar, baatoonee, sharmeelaa, mazaakiyaa…) — kind words only; the aunties are listening.
chapters.book4-L22:
Lesson 22 Getting Things Done (JugaaR)

The scene: Saturday, list in hand. A wedding is coming, which in Delhi means a tour of the neighborhood service economy: the darzee (tailor), the press-vaalaa at his ironing cart, the salon. Nobody does these things themselves — you get them done, and the grammar of getting-things-done is Unit 23's causative: -वाना -vaanaa. Today Jacob learns silvaanaa, kaTvaanaa, karvaanaa — and the mighty Delhi concept that holds it all together: जुगाड़ jugaaR [ju-gahR].

Dialogue: आज बहुत काम करवाने हैं aaj bahut kaam karvaane hain

Priya:
उठो! आज बहुत काम करवाने हैं।
uTho! aaj bahut kaam karvaane hain. [u-Thoh! ahj buh-hut kahm kur-vah-nay heh(n)]
Get up! We have a lot of things to get done today. (kaam (m pl) → karvaane hain — Unit 17 agreement on a Unit 23 verb)
Jacob:
करवाने हैं? मतलब — हम ख़ुद कुछ नहीं करेंगे?
karvaane hain? matlab — ham khud kuchh naheen karenge? [kur-vah-nay heh(n)? mut-lub — hum khud kuchh nuh-hee(n) kuh-ray(n)-gay]
GET done? Meaning — we ourselves won't do anything? (matlab (m) = meaning; khud = oneself)
Priya:
बिल्कुल! यह दिल्ली है, जान। यहाँ आधे काम ख़ुद नहीं किए जाते — करवाए जाते हैं।
bilkul! yeh dillee hai, jaan. yahaan aadhe kaam khud naheen kiye jaate — karvaae jaate hain. [bil-kul! yeh dil-lee heh, jahn. yuh-hah(n) ah-dhay kahm khud nuh-hee(n) ki-yeh jah-tay — kur-vah-ay jah-tay heh(n)]
Exactly! This is Delhi, jaan. Half the work here isn't done — it's gotten done. (jaan = "dear" (lit. life); note the Unit 23 passive: kiye jaate… karvaae jaate hain)
Priya:
(दर्ज़ी की दुकान पर) भैया, यह कपड़ा है — शादी के लिए एक कुर्ता सिलवाना है।
(darzee kee dukaan par) bhaiyaa, yeh kapRaa hai — shaadee ke liye ek kurtaa silvaanaa hai. [bheh-yah, yeh kup-Rah heh — shah-dee kay li-yeh ayk kur-tah sil-vah-nah heh]
(At the tailor's) Bhaiya, here's the fabric — we need a kurta stitched for a wedding.
Darzee:
ज़रूर, दीदी। मैं अभी नाप ले लेता हूँ। कब तक चाहिए?
zaroor, deedee. main abhee naap le letaa hoon. kab tak chaahiye? [zuh-roor, dee-dee. meh(n) uh-bhee nahp lay lay-tah hoo(n). kub tuk chah-hi-yay]
Of course, didi. I'll just take the measurements now. By when do you need it? (naap (m) measurement; le letaa hoon — "I'll just…", Unit 19)
Priya:
अगले संडे तक मिल जाएगा? शादी में पहनना है।
agle sanDe tak mil jaaegaa? shaadee mein pehnnaa hai. [ug-lay sun-Day tuk mil jah-ay-gah? shah-dee may(n) pehn-nah heh]
Will we have it by next Sunday? It's to be worn at the wedding.
Darzee:
हो जाएगा, दीदी। टेंशन मत लीजिए।
ho jaaegaa, deedee. Tenshan mat leejiye. [hoh jah-ay-gah, dee-dee. Ten-shun mut lee-ji-yay]
It'll get done, didi. Don't take tension. (the great Delhi promise, in its natural habitat)
Jacob (to Priya):
"हो जाएगा" का मतलब "हाँ" है या "शायद"?
"ho jaaegaa" kaa matlab "haan" hai yaa "shaayad"? [hoh jah-ay-gah kah mut-lub hah(n) heh yah shah-yud]
Does "ho jaaegaa" mean "yes" or "maybe"?
Priya:
मतलब है — "अगर तुम दो बार फ़ोन करोगे तो हो जाएगा।"
matlab hai — "agar tum do baar fon karoge to ho jaaegaa." [mut-lub heh — uh-gur tum doh bahr fohn kuh-roh-gay toh hoh jah-ay-gah]
It means — "if you call twice, it'll get done."
Jacob:
(प्रेस वाले के पास) भैया, ये पाँच कपड़े — इस्त्री कर दीजिए। शाम तक हो जाएँगे?
(pres vaale ke paas) bhaiyaa, ye paanch kapRe — istree kar deejiye. shaam tak ho jaaenge? [bheh-yah, yay pah(n)ch kup-Ray — ist-ree kur dee-ji-yay. shahm tuk hoh jah-ay(n)-gay]
(At the press-vaalaa's cart) Bhaiya, these five clothes — please iron them. Will they be done by evening? (istree (f) = iron, ironing)
Press-vaalaa:
हो जाएँगे, साहब। दस रुपये कपड़ा।
ho jaaenge, saahab. das rupaye kapRaa. [hoh jah-ay(n)-gay, sah-hub. dus ru-puh-yay kup-Rah]
They'll be done, sir. Ten rupees a piece.
Jacob:
(सैलून में) भैया, बाल कटवाने हैं। ज़्यादा छोटे मत करना।
(sailoon mein) bhaiyaa, baal kaTvaane hain. zyaadaa chhoTe mat karnaa. [bheh-yah, bahl kuT-vah-nay heh(n). zyah-dah chhoh-Tay mut kur-nah]
(At the salon) Bhaiya, I need a haircut. Don't make it too short. (baal (m pl) → kaTvaane hain)
Naaee:
जी साहब। चंपी भी करवा लीजिए — सिर्फ़ पचास रुपये। दिमाग़ खुल जाएगा!
jee saahab. champee bhee karvaa leejiye — sirf pachaas rupaye. dimaag khul jaaegaa! [jee sah-hub. chum-pee bhee kur-vah lee-ji-yay — sirf puh-chahs ru-puh-yay. di-mahg khul jah-ay-gah]
Yes sir. Get a champi (head massage) too — only fifty rupees. It'll open up your brain! (champee (f); dimaag (m) brain; karvaa leejiye — causative + vector, double-decker verb)
Jacob (later, blissful):
वाह! अब समझा। दिल्ली में सब कुछ हो जाता है — बस पता होना चाहिए कि किससे करवाना है।
vaah! ab samjhaa. dillee mein sab kuchh ho jaataa hai — bas pataa honaa chaahiye ki kisse karvaanaa hai. [vah! ub sum-jhah. dil-lee may(n) sub kuchh hoh jah-tah heh — bus puh-tah hoh-nah chah-hi-yay ki kis-say kur-vah-nah heh]
Wow! Now I get it. In Delhi everything gets done — you just have to know who to get it done by.
Priya:
इसी को जुगाड़ कहते हैं, जान! …और हाँ — वह चंपी नाई का जुगाड़ था, तुम्हारी जेब पर।
isee ko jugaaR kehte hain, jaan! …aur haan — voh champee naaee kaa jugaaR thaa, tumhaaree jeb par. [i-see koh ju-gahR keh-tay heh(n), jahn! awr hah(n) — voh chum-pee nah-ee kah ju-gahR thah, tum-hah-ree jayb pur]
THAT is what they call jugaaR, dear! …And by the way — that champi was the barber's jugaaR, on your pocket. (naaee (m) barber; jeb (f) pocket)

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
दर्ज़ीdarzee (m)dur-zeetailor
नाईnaaee (m)nah-eebarber
मिस्त्रीmistree (m)mist-reemechanic, repairman
सिलवानाsilvaanaa (vt)sil-vah-nahto have (clothes) stitched
बाल कटवानाbaal kaTvaanaabahl kuT-vah-nahto get a haircut
करवाना / करानाkarvaanaa / karaanaa (vt)kur-vah-nah / kuh-rah-nahto get (something) done
इस्त्री करवानाistree karvaanaaist-ree kur-vah-nahto get the ironing done (istree (f))
ठीक करवानाTheek karvaanaaTheek kur-vah-nahto get (something) fixed
कब तक चाहिए?kab tak chaahiye?kub tuk chah-hi-yayby when do you need it?

जुगाड़jugaaR (m)ju-gahRthe creative workaround (see box)
चंपीchampee (f)chum-peehead massage

Do it — or get it done

You do it (vt)You get it doneSay itExample
करना karnaaकरवाना karvaanaakur-vah-nahइस्त्री करवा लो।
बनाना banaanaaबनवाना banvaanaabun-vah-nahहलवाई से मिठाई बनवाओ।
काटना kaaTnaaकटवाना kaTvaanaakuT-vah-nahबाल कटवा लो।
सीना seenaaसिलवाना silvaanaasil-vah-nahदर्ज़ी से कुर्ता सिलवाओ।
धोना dhonaaधुलवाना dhulvaanaadhul-vah-nahगाड़ी धुलवा लो।

Name the professional with se: दर्ज़ी से सिलवाओ darzee se silvaao, मिस्त्री से ठीक करवाओ mistree se Theek karvaao — done by his hands, arranged by you.

Self or hired hands — the verb tells all, so pick carefully. मैंने बाल काटे maine baal kaaTe means you personally wielded the scissors (alarming). "I got a haircut" is मैंने बाल कटवाए। maine baal kaTvaae. [meh(n)-nay bahl kuT-vah-ay] Same trap with कुर्ता सिया / सिलवाया and खाना बनाया / बनवाया. If a professional was involved, the verb needs its -vaa-. (And yes — causatives are transitive, so past tense takes ne.)

Causatives love to stack with Unit 19 vectors: करवा लो karvaa lo "get it done (and pocket the result)," सिलवा लेना silvaa lenaa "do get it stitched (when you get a chance)," बनवा दीजिए banvaa deejiye "please have it made (for me)." Double-decker verbs — causative for who works, vector for the flavor — are peak spoken Delhi. If you can say चंपी करवा लीजिए and mean it, Unit 23 is yours.

जुगाड़ jugaaR is Delhi's superpower: the creative, semi-official workaround that gets a thing done when the normal route is closed. The mistree who revives your scooter with wire and confidence; the cousin who "knows a guy" at the office (सेटिंग है seTing hai [say-Ting heh] "there's an arrangement"); the printer fixed with a rubber band until Tuesday. Verb form included: जुगाड़ करना / लगाना — कोई जुगाड़ करो यार! koee jugaaR karo yaar! "figure something out, yaar!" It isn't cheating — it's engineering with charm, and Delhi runs on it.

The darzee, the press-vaalaa and the naaee aren't vendors; they're relationships. The press-vaalaa's cart (Lesson 5's morning soundtrack) irons the whole block's clothes at a fixed rupees-per-piece rate and knows everyone's schedule. The family darzee has stitched three generations of wedding outfits and keeps everyone's naap on file. Loyalty is repaid at Diwali with sweets and a bonus — and in emergencies: a true family darzee will produce a kurta overnight for a wedding, grumbling magnificently the whole time.

Comprehension

Exercise 22A — Answer in Hindi

Full sentences. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 22.

  1. प्रिया दर्ज़ी से क्या सिलवाना चाहती है? (Priya darzee se kyaa silvaanaa chaahtee hai?)
  2. कुर्ता कब तक चाहिए? (kurtaa kab tak chaahiye?)
  3. जैकब प्रेस वाले से क्या करवाता है? (Jacob pres vaale se kyaa karvaataa hai?)
  4. इस्त्री का क्या भाव है? (istree kaa kyaa bhaav hai?)
  5. नाई के हिसाब से चंपी से क्या होगा? (naaee ke hisaab se champee se kyaa hogaa?)

Pattern drill: from doing to getting done

Exercise 22B — Add the -vaa-

Items 1–6: rewrite so the subject GETS it done (add the se-agent where given). Items 7–8: turn the command into a causative command with a vector (karvaa lo style). Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 22.

  1. मैं कपड़े धोता हूँ। (main kapRe dhotaa hoon.)
  2. मैंने कुर्ता सिया। (maine kurtaa siyaa.) [darzee se]
  3. मैंने बाल काटे। (maine baal kaaTe.)
  4. हम खाना बनाते हैं। (ham khaanaa banaate hain.) [halvaaee se]
  5. उसने घर साफ़ किया। (usne ghar saaf kiyaa.)
  6. मैं गाड़ी ठीक करता हूँ। (main gaaRee Theek kartaa hoon.) [mistree se]
  7. कपड़े इस्त्री करो। (kapRe istree karo.) → [+ lenaa]
  8. बाल काटो। (baal kaaTo.) → [get a haircut, + lenaa]

Translation practice

Exercise 22C — Into Hindi

Decide each time: do, make, or get done? Write Devanagari and roman. Answers: Answer Key, Lesson 22.

  1. I want to have a kurta stitched for the wedding.
  2. I get my hair cut every month.
  3. Get the car fixed by the mechanic. (tum)
  4. Don't worry — it'll get done by tomorrow.

Exercise 22D — Into English

  1. मैंने अपनी शादी का कुर्ता इसी दर्ज़ी से सिलवाया था। (maine apnee shaadee kaa kurtaa isee darzee se silvaayaa thaa.)
  2. भैया, ज़्यादा छोटे मत करना — थोड़े ही काटना। (bhaiyaa, zyaadaa chhoTe mat karnaa — thoRe hee kaaTnaa.)
  3. दिल्ली में जो काम पैसे से नहीं होता, वह जुगाड़ से हो जाता है। (dillee mein jo kaam paise se naheen hotaa, voh jugaaR se ho jaataa hai.)
  4. चंपी करवा लो साहब — दिमाग़ खुल जाएगा! (champee karvaa lo saahab — dimaag khul jaaegaa!)

Roleplay: errand marathon. Write a real five-errand list, then work the room: your partner plays darzee, press-vaalaa, naaee and mistree in turn (props encouraged). For each stop you must (1) state the job with a causative — …सिलवाना है / करवाने हैं, (2) pin the deadline — कब तक हो जाएगा?, (3) settle the price, and (4) when she answers हो जाएगा, push back like a local: पक्का? या दो बार फ़ोन करूँ? Then swap. Real-world quest: this week, get one actual thing done with a -vaanaa verb — ironing, a haircut, a repair — and report the whole saga in Hindi, jugaaR included.
chapters.book4-L23:
Lesson 23 Phone Call Home & Gossip

The scene: 9 p.m. — which in a Delhi family means one thing: the phone rings, and it's Mummy. Tonight's call has everything: welfare checks, a Diwali invitation, and premium neighborhood news. This is Unit 20's reported speech in the wild — मम्मी कह रही थीं कि… mummy keh rahee theen ki… [mum-mee keh ruh-hee thee(n) ki] — where Hindi does something English never does: it keeps the speaker's original tense. Jacob's job tonight: catch the news and relay the messages.

Dialogue: मम्मी का फ़ोन mummy kaa fon

Priya (answering):
हाँ मम्मी, नमस्ते! जी, सब ठीक है। …हाँ, यहीं हैं। लीजिए, बात कीजिए।
haan mummy, namaste! jee, sab Theek hai. …haan, yaheen hain. leejiye, baat keejiye. [hah(n) mum-mee, nuh-muhs-tay! jee, sub Theek heh. hah(n), yuh-hee(n) heh(n). lee-ji-yay, baht kee-ji-yay]
Yes Mummy, namaste! Yes, all's well. …Yes, he's right here. Here, talk to him.
Jacob:
नमस्ते मम्मी जी! कैसी हैं आप?
namaste mummy jee! kaisee hain aap? [nuh-muhs-tay mum-mee jee! keh-see heh(n) ahp]
Namaste Mummy-ji! How are you?
Mummy (on the phone):
ख़ुश रहो, बेटा! मैं ठीक हूँ। आप खाना ठीक से खा रहे हैं न?
khush raho, beTaa! main Theek hoon. aap khaanaa Theek se khaa rahe hain na? [khush ruh-hoh, bay-Tah! meh(n) Theek hoo(n). ahp khah-nah Theek say khah ruh-hay heh(n) nah]
Stay happy, son! I'm fine. You're eating properly, aren't you? (mother-in-law priorities, in order)
Jacob:
जी मम्मी जी! रोज़ दाल-रोटी… और कभी-कभी मोमोज़।
jee mummy jee! roz daal-roTee… aur kabhee-kabhee momos. [jee mum-mee jee! rohz dahl-roh-Tee… awr kuh-bhee kuh-bhee moh-mohz]
Yes Mummy-ji! Daal-roti every day… and sometimes momos.
Mummy (laughing):
अच्छा बेटा, अब प्रिया को फ़ोन दो।
achchhaa beTaa, ab Priya ko fon do. [uch-chhah bay-Tah, ub pri-yah koh fohn doh]
All right son, now give the phone to Priya.
Priya:
हाँ मम्मी… क्या?! सच में?! कब?! …(जैकब से) सुनो —
मम्मी कह रही थीं कि शर्मा आंटी के बेटे की सगाई हो गई!
haan mummy… kyaa?! sach mein?! kab?! …(Jacob se) suno — mummy keh rahee theen ki Sharmaa aunty ke beTe kee sagaaee ho gaee! [hah(n) mum-mee… kyah?! such may(n)?! kub?! su-noh — mum-mee keh ruh-hee thee(n) ki shur-mah ahn-Tee kay bay-Tay kee suh-gah-ee hoh guh-ee]
Yes Mummy… what?! Really?! When?! …(to Jacob) Listen — Mummy was saying that Sharma aunty's son got engaged! (sagaaee (f) engagement; the ki-clause keeps Mummy's own tense: ho gaee)
Jacob:
वही आंटी जो सबके लिए रिश्ते ढूँढती हैं?
vahee aunty jo sabke liye rishte DhoonDhtee hain? [vuh-hee ahn-Tee joh sub-kay li-yay rish-tay Dhoo(n)Dh-tee heh(n)]
The same aunty who hunts matches for everyone else? (DhoonDhnaa = to search for; Lesson 21 pays off)
Priya:
वही! और सुनो — रोहन ने बताया कि वह अगले हफ़्ते मुंबई से आ रहा है।
vahee! aur suno — Rohan ne bataayaa ki voh agle hafte mumbaee se aa rahaa hai. [vuh-hee! awr su-noh — roh-hun nay buh-tah-yah ki voh ug-lay huf-tay mum-buh-ee say ah ruh-hah heh]
The very same! And listen — Rohan said (told them) that he's coming from Mumbai next week. (his words were "main aa rahaa hoon" — the tense stays)
Mummy (through the phone, loudly):
और प्रिया — पूछो जैकब से, दिवाली पर आ रहे हो न तुम दोनों?
aur Priya — poochho Jacob se, divaalee par aa rahe ho na tum donon? [awr pri-yah — poo-chhoh jay-kub say, di-vah-lee pur ah ruh-hay hoh nah tum doh-noh(n)]
And Priya — ask Jacob, you two are coming for Diwali, right? (donon = both)
Jacob (loudly, toward the phone):
मम्मी जी, हम ज़रूर आएँगे!
mummy jee, ham zaroor aaenge! [mum-mee jee, hum zuh-roor ah-ay(n)-gay]
Mummy-ji, we will definitely come!
Mummy:
सुन लिया! और जैकब से कहना कि इस बार मैं उसे अपने हाथ के छोले-भटूरे खिलाऊँगी।
sun liyaa! aur Jacob se kehnaa ki is baar main use apne haath ke chhole-bhaTure khilaaoongee. [sun li-yah! awr jay-kub say keh-nah ki is bahr meh(n) u-say up-nay hahth kay chhoh-lay bhuh-Too-ray khi-lah-oo(n)-gee]
Heard it! And tell Jacob that this time I'll feed him chhole bhature made with my own hands. (khilaanaa — the love-causative from Unit 23)
Jacob (to Priya):
मम्मी जी से कहना कि मैं अभी से भूखा हूँ!
mummy jee se kehnaa ki main abhee se bhookhaa hoon! [mum-mee jee say keh-nah ki meh(n) uh-bhee say bhoo-khah hoo(n)]
Tell Mummy-ji that I'm hungry already! (message relayed straight back — X se kehnaa ki…)
Priya:
सुना आपने? …अच्छा मम्मी, अब रखती हूँ। कल फिर बात करेंगे।
sunaa aapne? …achchhaa mummy, ab rakhtee hoon. kal phir baat karenge. [su-nah ahp-nay? uch-chhah mum-mee, ub rukh-tee hoo(n). kul fir baht kuh-ray(n)-gay]
Did you hear him? …Okay Mummy, I'll hang up now. We'll talk again tomorrow. (rakhtee hoon, lit. "I'm putting (it) down" — the standard sign-off)
Mummy:
ठीक है बेटा। अपना ख़याल रखना, दोनों।
Theek hai beTaa. apnaa khayaal rakhnaa, donon. [Theek heh bay-Tah. up-nah khuh-yahl rukh-nah, doh-noh(n)]
All right, beta. Take care of yourselves, both of you. (khayaal (m) care; apnaa khayaal rakhnaa — the warm goodbye)
Jacob (after the call):
तुम्हारी मम्मी हर बार पूछती हैं कि मैंने खाना खाया या नहीं। क्यों?
tumhaaree mummy har baar poochhtee hain ki maine khaanaa khaayaa yaa naheen. kyon? [tum-hah-ree mum-mee hur bahr poochh-tee heh(n) ki meh(n)-nay khah-nah khah-yah yah nuh-hee(n). kyoh(n)]
Your mom asks every single time whether I've eaten or not. Why?
Priya:
क्योंकि वे तुमसे प्यार करती हैं, इसलिए!
kyonki voh tumse pyaar kartee hain, isliye! [kyoh(n)-ki voh tum-say pyahr kur-tee heh(n), is-li-yay]
Because she loves you — that's why! (in mom language, "khaanaa khaayaa?" IS "I love you")

The tense-freeze rule, highlighted. Hindi reports speech in the speaker's original tense — no English-style backshift. Rohan's words: "मैं आ रहा हूँ।" Report: रोहन ने बताया कि वह आ रहा है। Rohan ne bataayaa ki voh aa rahaa hai. English says "he said he was coming," but writing ✗ …कि वह आ रहा था changes the meaning to "he was coming back then (and maybe isn't anymore)." Swap the pronouns, pipe it through कि ki, and leave the tense exactly where the speaker put it. Every time.

Key phrases

हिन्दीRomanSay itMeaning
…कह रही थीं कि……keh rahee theen ki…keh ruh-hee thee(n) ki(she) was saying that… (respect pl)
उसने बताया कि…usne bataayaa ki…us-nay buh-tah-yah kihe/she told (us) that…
उन्होंने पूछा कि…unhonne poochhaa ki…un-hoh(n)-nay poo-chhah kithey/she (resp.) asked whether…
…से कहना कि……se kehnaa ki…say keh-nah kitell (X) that… (message relay)
सगाईsagaaee (f)suh-gah-eeengagement
